It constructs parent-conditioned candidate trees from one backbone pass and replays their expansion, pruning, and budgeted packing during training. Survival negative log-likelihood weights retained edges by reference-derived path mass, while a capped coverage hinge promotes target-important alternatives near local selection boundaries. Both objectives reuse reference-chain target distributions without additional target forward passes. We evaluate greedy decoding with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B on nine general benchmarks and six writing domains. Across targets and suites, TreeSpark improves mean acceptance length over DSpark by 23.4% to 31.6% and mean single-request throughput by 15.1% to 25.0%. Batched Qwen3-4B throughput improves by 12.6% to 17.2%. At fixed attention capacity and inference policy, the proposed supervision further improves mean acceptance length by approximately 6.4% and mean system throughput by 4.2% to 5.0% on Qwen3-4B.

title: Reciprocal Dynamics in Congruence Jumping: Integral Orbits and Valuation Cones
abstract: For fixed positive degrees $n,m$, alternating monic reciprocal transformations define a rational discrete dynamical system on the finite-dimensional coefficient space of polynomial pairs. This system arises from congruence jumping in polynomial divisibility problems, where a quotient move changes the polynomial state, but its coefficient dynamics can be studied independently. We prove that every state with nonzero constant terms returns after four alternating updates to its rational gauge classes and classify when this return orbit is realized over $\mathbb Z$. The local obstruction is encoded by endpoint $p$-adic valuation defects. After the first integral block, constant-term valuations evolve by an explicit matrix $M_{n,m}\in\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb Z)$ whose trace depends only on $s=nm$. This yields a finite-order, elliptic-type regime for $s<4$, a parabolic dilation regime for $s=4$, and a hyperbolic regime for $s>4$. In the hyperbolic case, invariant thresholds, irrational eigencones, and discrete valley formulas give finite criteria for forward and bi-infinite integral orbits; nevertheless, failure can be delayed arbitrarily long. At the pointwise level, separated auxiliary-relation transport factors through the jumped-variable projection. One jump preserves the visible support rank, while two alternating jumps collapse it to dimension at most one; saturation cannot restore rank. In the quadratic specialization, a rank-two $p$-adic relation lattice gives an exact local cancellation-depth formula and a finite criterion on periodic Vieta orbits. We classify the fixed auxiliary relations that saturate indefinitely on an irreducible six-cycle and construct arbitrarily long persistence on parabolic and fixed hyperbolic orbits.

title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
abstract: A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $ε$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}ε.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $ε$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative Kähler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative Kähler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, Hörmander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.

title: Entropic Inequalities and Limit Theorems in Boolean Probability
abstract: We study Boolean entropy and Fisher information in information inequalities and the Boolean central limit theorem. We prove a fractional Stam inequality for the Boolean Fisher information associated with arbitrary fractional partitions of subset sums, and derive an entropy power inequality for sums of Boolean independent random variables and its weighted version. We then establish a Boolean analogue of Barron's entropy convergence result along the Boolean central limit theorem: Boolean entropy converges to the entropy of the Rademacher law if and only if the initial entropy is finite. Furthermore, under a finite fourth moment, in the Boolean central limit theorem, we obtain \[ Γ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b)= \frac{m_4(μ)-1-m_3(μ)^2}{2}\frac{\log n}{n} +o\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \] with an explicit example showing sharpness. For symmetric laws with finite fourth moment and finite Boolean Fisher information, \[ Ψ(μ_n\mid\mathbf b) =2\bigl(m_4(μ)-1\bigr)\frac{\log n}{n} +o\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right). \] Our approach is based on the Nevanlinna representation of Cauchy transforms.

title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
abstract: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.

title: Finite Modular Hamiltonians and Their Singular Limits
abstract: Using the open solid torus as a finite parent, we revisit modular flow for spherical regions in conformal field theory. Its nonsingular angular evolution gives finite modular generators in a very simple form, while an exact conformal map to a cavity frame recovers the Rindler, CHM, and stationary-source ball constructions as singular limits. The same finite parent also provides a regular completion of the center obstruction in the complexified ball flow. Charged, Dirac, and inhomogeneous scalar examples are given.

title: Noise-Aware Lombard Speech Synthesis via Flow-GRPO for Intelligibility Optimization
abstract: Voice-based conversational agents are increasingly deployed in real-world settings, where environmental noise often degrades the interactive experience. Therefore, robust acoustic adaptability is essential to maintain natural and intelligible human-computer communication. However, most existing systems remain acoustically insensitive and fail to emulate the human Lombard effect, in which speakers involuntarily adjust their vocal production to preserve intelligibility in the presence of noise. As a result, their communicative reliability degrades under adverse acoustic conditions. To remain intelligible in noisy environments, conversational agents require a mechanism to emulate noise-induced adaptive behavior during synthesis. We propose NIL-TTS, a noise-induced Lombard TTS framework. We integrate a feature-wise linear modulation (FiLM) mechanism into a flow-matching backbone for dynamic vocal adaptation. A two-stage training paradigm is utilized: initial supervised fine-tuning on paired Lombard corpora, followed by Flow-GRPO post-training to optimize for intelligibility. Evaluations confirm that NIL-TTS autonomously adjusts its output in response to varying noise conditions, exhibiting key correlates of the human Lombard effect. Driven by these adaptive modulations, the synthesized speech achieves significant intelligibility improvements that scale proportionally with noise intensity. Ultimately, this work presents a flow-matching and reinforcement learning-based advancement within the adaptive Lombard speech synthesis paradigm for challenging real-world scenarios.

title: New bounds for $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ shifted convolution sums
abstract: Shifted convolution sums of $\mathrm{GL}(3)\times\mathrm{GL}(2)$ type have been extensively studied in several important settings, while a number of natural cases remain open. In this paper, we first revisit the shifted convolution sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and the divisor function $d(n)$, improving the recent power saving of $1/42$ obtained by Blomer and Li to $1/22$. We also treat the corresponding sums involving $λ_π(1,n)$ and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$, settling a previously open case and obtaining a power saving of $1/22$. Here $λ_π(1,n)$ denotes the normalized Fourier coefficients of a Hecke--Maass cusp form $π$ on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\mathbb{Z})$, and $r(n,\mathcal{Q})$ denotes the number of representations of a positive integer $n$ by a positive definite integral binary quadratic form $\mathcal{Q}$. The proof combines two circle methods with a different organization of the major-arc analysis. A key point is that the nonzero Poisson frequencies are kept together in a single coefficient vector, rather than estimated separately, which allows them to be controlled by a finite matrix norm. The zero Poisson frequency is treated separately: its contribution is independent of the reduced residue class, and its arithmetic mean cancels the constant term in the complementary Jutila weight before absolute values are taken. We make this cancellation explicit, including the relevant normalization and local factors. The same mechanism extends to the binary quadratic-form setting, while the remaining Jutila contribution is handled by the available correlation estimates.

title: Macdonald dual in the semilocal case and applications to local homology and local cohomology
abstract: This paper extends Macdonald's duality theory and Cuong-Nam's local homology theory -- which is in some sense dual to the local cohomology theory of A. Grothendieck [Gro1] -- to semilocal noetherian rings equipped with the $J$-adic topology. By overcoming the key structural obstructions of the semilocal setting via Zöschinger's structure theory and semilocal Matlis duality, this work establishes topological limit duality isomorphisms and links local homology with local cohomology. Ultimately, this framework provides the foundational machinery required to extend the classical results of Macdonald [Mac] and Cuong-Nam [C-N1] to the semilocal setting.

title: Galaxy-to-galaxy stochasticity has a limited impact on reionization and the 21-cm signal at fixed mean emissivity
abstract: Galaxy-to-galaxy stochasticity may be less important for reionization, IGM heating, and the 21-cm signal than commonly assumed. We find that most of its apparent impact arises because introducing or removing scatter changes the mean emissivity of the galaxy population, rather than from redistributing radiation at fixed mean emissivity. We use the Meraxes semi-analytic model to separate these effects. For ionising sources, we vary the scatter in the escape fraction and in the SFR-halo mass relation across three source prescriptions. For the X-ray heating sources, we introduce luminosity scatter and also separately remove SFR scatter. Without recalibration, these modifications shift the mean emissivities, changing the timing of reionization and IGM heating and producing substantial differences in the 21-cm signal. Once the relevant mean emissivities are restored, however, the global ionizing and thermal histories converge and the power-spectrum differences fall below the forecast sensitivity of a deep SKA-Low observation. There are some weak changes in ionisation morphology, depending on which galaxies dominate the ionising emissivity and on their response to photoheating. Within the models and scales considered here, calibrating the mean radiative emissivities is therefore substantially more important than resolving their galaxy-to-galaxy scatter.

title: Radar-Only Long-Term Beam Prediction in mmWave Vehicular Networks: An Empirical Study of Doppler Input and Cross-Modal Distillation
abstract: Sensing-aided beam prediction could cut the beam-training overhead of millimeter-wave vehicular links, and two design choices could strengthen a radar-only predictor: a Doppler-resolved input and knowledge distilled from a camera during training. We measure what each is worth in received power rather than in top-1 accuracy, whose differences of a few points amount to only tenths of a decibel. We use real DeepSense 6G measurements, mainly at one roadside site, and one convolutional-recurrent predictor family evaluated open-loop up to 0.67 s ahead. Adding a range-Doppler map to the range-angle map lowers the mean beam-selection loss by 0.28 dB (95% bootstrap interval [0.14, 0.41]). The gain comes from the Doppler content, not from the extra input, and replicates, as pre-specified, at a second base station, although holding the last measured beam beats both predictors there. Cross-modal knowledge distillation from a motion-mask vision-radar teacher, by contrast, changes received power by -0.01 dB ([-0.07, +0.06]). The tested teacher, student, fusion and distillation variants show the same null in the metric each was scored on. Where distillation helps, in an exploratory run with few training passes, a radar-only teacher trained on all training passes reproduces most of the gain. For this predictor family and the full training set, the measurable gain at the link comes from Doppler-resolved radar content; no tested route for transferring training-only visual information adds a resolved gain.

title: When Occupation-derived Skills Don't Help: On the Limits of Skill-Augmented Career Path Prediction
abstract: Skills are widely assumed to play a central role in career transitions, motivating their use in career path prediction (CPP) systems. In this work, we critically examine whether explicit skill representations provide complementary signal beyond text-based job representations. We evaluate multiple strategies for incorporating skills into CPP models, including score fusion and neural architectures, under two conditions: predicted skills and ground-truth ESCO annotations. Surprisingly, across two benchmark datasets, none of these settings yield substantial improvements over strong text-only baselines. Even when using ground-truth skills, gains remain marginal and inconsistent. Through detailed analysis, we identify key factors underlying this result: high redundancy between textual and skill representations, limited discriminative power of ESCO's taxonomy, and representational collapse in skill embeddings. Furthermore, we find that skill prediction difficulty correlates with overall sample difficulty, limiting the potential for complementary signals. Our findings challenge the common assumption that explicit skill modeling inherently benefits career prediction and suggest that dense text representations already capture most skill-relevant information.

title: Dimension-Optimal Dynamic Regret in Exp-Concave Online Learning
abstract: Tracking changing comparators is a central problem in online learning. For exp-concave losses, previous work established the $T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3}$ dependence on the horizon $T$ and Euclidean path length $P_T$ for fixed dimension, while the optimal cost of dimension remained unresolved. We resolve this question by establishing a sharp $d^{1/3}$ curved dimension factor, improving the $d^{2/3}$ factor of recent switching and interval reductions [1, 2]. To achieve this improvement, we develop a proper, full-information learner on compact convex subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ that adapts to the unknown path length and, under fixed dimension-independent diameter, gradient, and curvature parameters, guarantees $$\operatorname{Reg}_T(u_{1:T}) \le \widetilde{O}\left(d+\min\left\{d^{1/3}T^{1/3}P_T^{2/3},\sqrt{TP_T},T\right\}\right).$$ A matching lower bound on a diameter-one Euclidean ball establishes the minimax frontier up to logarithmic factors when $T\gtrsim d^2$, including the transition from the curved rate to larger path budgets. The lower bound already holds for losses that depend on only one coordinate per round, isolating an unavoidable cost of learning across directions. Our upper bound follows from square-root Gaussian KL control of comparator movement and a cancellation argument that pays for history restarts. The curved learner maintains $O(\log^2 T)$ Gaussian states, uses one gradient per round, and runs in time near-linear in $T$ under a Mahalanobis-projection oracle.

title: Asymmetry and Complexity of Nondeterministic Computations
abstract: Symmetry of Information (SoI) [ZL70] is a fundamental theorem of classical Kolmogorov complexity whose status for time-bounded computation is closely related to central open problems in complexity theory and cryptography. In a recent development, [HMO26] showed that SoI fails for $rKt$ complexity, namely in the setting of randomized computation. By contrast, many basic properties of Kolmogorov complexity are known to remain valid in the presence of nondeterminism [HLO26], suggesting that SoI may provide a fruitful structural principle for exploring the relative power of randomness and nondeterminism in computation. Our results reveal that the validity of SoI for nondeterministic computation, namely for $nKt$ complexity, is a subtle question connected to several frontiers. We show that symmetry of information holds on average for randomized extensions of $nKt$, while its worst case validity would imply breakthrough complexity separations. Although the standard cryptographic argument for asymmetry does not extend to the nondeterministic setting, we provide evidence that information remains asymmetric in nondeterministic computations. Among other results, we show that SoI would imply a collapse of exponential time classes to low levels of the polynomial hierarchy. Then, building on the work of [Hir22b, GK22, KK26, HMO26], we develop a general framework connecting symmetry of information, meta-complexity, and explicit constructions in the nondeterministic setting. More precisely, we prove that suitable formulations of these three notions are quantitatively equivalent. We apply different aspects of this correspondence to make progress on complexity lower bounds and on the failure of SoI for nondeterministic computation. These consequences are unconditional and provide some of the strongest known lower bounds in meta-complexity.

title: From Single-Particle Thermal Asymmetry to Collective Control: Janus Plasmonic Colloids for Photothermal Applications
abstract: Janus nanoheaters provide a route to break the spatial symmetry of thermoplasmonic heating and generate directionally biased thermal gradients at the nanoscale. However, in realistic photothermal scenarios, nanoheaters rarely act as isolated objects, but rather operate within colloidal assemblies where collective thermal and electromagnetic effects reshape the local temperature landscape. Here, we investigate how the intrinsic thermal asymmetry of a single Janus plasmonic nanoheater is transformed when moving from isolated particles to planar random arrays under continuous-wave illumination. Using coupled electromagnetic and steady-state heat-transfer simulations, we first quantify the finite spatial range over which the single-particle Janus signature remains detectable. We show that neighboring nanoheaters introduce two competing effects: a nearly symmetric collective thermal background that screens and homogenizes the Janus factor, and short-range neighbor-induced asymmetries that partially compensate this screening when interparticle distances become comparable to the spatial extent of the single-particle thermal anisotropy. We derive a closed-form analytical model for the array-averaged Janus factor as a function of nanoparticle number and surface density. The model predicts the screening-dominated regime from single-particle quantities and identifies deviations associated with near-field neighbor-induced contributions at higher densities. These results demonstrate a central trade-off for biomedical photothermal applications in continuous-wave operation: collective heating is required to reach relevant temperature increments, but it progressively erases the directional Janus character by thermal homogenization. Our framework provides a practical route to predict and rationally design the spatial temperature distribution in plasmonic assemblies of Janus particles.

title: Value-Guided Repulsion for Offline Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Drifting models have emerged as a highly efficient and stable paradigm for policy design in offline reinforcement learning (RL). However, standard drift policies determine repulsion solely from geometric relationships among generated actions and therefore cannot distinguish them by expected value. To address this limitation, we introduce Value-Guided Repulsion Q-Learning (VRQL) to integrate action value estimates into the particle interaction field. For each state, VRQL combines geometric kernel distance with a normalized Q value scaling. This mechanism assigns greater repulsive influence to particles with lower values while strictly retaining attraction toward behavior action. Consequently, this value-guided interaction field aligns behavior regularization with policy improvement without adding an auxiliary behavior model stage. On 50 OGBench task configurations and 6 D4RL AntMaze configurations, VRQL demonstrates highly competitive performance against established baselines, suggesting that value-guided particle interaction is an effective method for offline RL.

title: HEM-Med: A Hierarchical Agentic Memory Framework for Safe Multi-Center Medication Recommendation
abstract: Medication recommendation (MR) is critical for clinical decision support. While existing MR methods are mostly designed for single-center learning, where only one independent hospital is involved, multi-center MR with hospitals of different scales has become increasingly demanding in practice. In multi center settings, abundant data from large medical centers can improve recommendation performance for low-resource centers. Despite a few preliminary attempts on this task, two critical gaps remain. Gap 1: Existing multi-center methods fail to disentangle transferable cross-hospital clinical experience from hospital-specific prescribing patterns, limiting clinical feasibility and physician acceptance. Gap 2: They commonly overlook multi label safety constraints of MR, including drug-drug interaction risks and local formulary feasibility, which are essential for safe real-world deployment. To address these gaps, we propose HEM-Med, a novel hierarchical agentic memory framework for multi-center MR. To address Gap 1, we design a disentangled hierarchical memory module that builds patient-level medication context attribution records and disentangles them into cross hospital experience memory and hospital-specific residual memory. To address Gap 2, we introduce a safety-aware medication set generation module, which integrates dual-level experience retrieval with safety-aware set decoding to produce clinically relevant, safer, and locally adaptive medication recommendations. Experiments on a real-world multi-center eICU dataset show that HEM-Med outperforms representative transfer learning, LLM-based, and MR baselines in terms of both recommendation accuracy and safety.

title: Old structures, a vanishing formula
abstract: We identify a normalization defect in a determinantal construction of fourth-order Hahn difference equations and compare its scalar equation with Foupouagnigni's 1998 elimination and its published 2001 counterpart. On an explicit positive orthogonal family, all five prescribed coefficients vanish: the formula gives \(0=0\) and imposes no condition. Along an explicit regular perturbation, division by \(\varepsilon^2\) before specialization recovers a nonzero equation on that family, the same scalar equation as the correctly executed old shift-and-eliminate procedure. On the common nondegenerate domain specified below, both constructions give the same scalar operator up to a nonzero rational factor. The first-order degree bounds follow directly from valid identities of 1998; preserving cancellations gives a bound that can be arbitrarily sharper on explicit admissible inputs, together with exact top coefficients and cancellation criteria. Explicit coefficient formulas do not by themselves yield a new scalar equation on this domain. Our comparison does not exclude corrective or expository contributions; additional computational gain or exceptional coverage must be demonstrated.

title: SWE-Stream: Scaling Executable Training Data for SWE Agents via Progressive Construction and Elastic Streaming
abstract: Software engineering agents have advanced rapidly, but scaling their training remains constrained by the limited availability of high-quality executable tasks. Development histories contain valuable signals for constructing such tasks, yet they often require substantial reconstruction due to incomplete environments, missing tests, and inconsistent artifacts. We present SWE-Stream, a system for scaling executable SWE training data through progressive construction and elastic streaming execution. SWE-Stream progressively validates and refines task candidates, reusing existing artifacts when possible and applying targeted completion only when necessary. An elastic scheduler asynchronously coordinates construction stages under shared resource constraints, adapting execution budgets based on observed workload demands. Using development histories from 10,728 repositories across six programming languages, SWE-Stream constructs 80,874 validated tasks and collects 118,688 successful trajectories. Fine-tuning Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507 on these trajectories achieves resolve rates of 69.0%, 49.3%, and 45.42% on SWE-bench Verified, Multilingual, and Pro, respectively. In a controlled comparison with approximately matched training budgets, SWE-Stream achieves a 45.6% resolve rate on SWE-bench Verified, outperforming three existing data sources. Moreover, its streaming construction strategy improves efficiency, delivering $1.45\times$ the accepted-task throughput of batch construction and accepting 13.2% more tasks than fixed-limit streaming.

title: Revisiting the Optical F-corona from the Artemis II Total Solar Eclipse with RAW Data: How Far Can Consumer JPEG Images Be Trusted for Astronomical Photometry?
abstract: We reanalyze the total solar eclipse images taken with a consumer camera during the Artemis II lunar flyby, using the RAW data as ground truth for our previous analysis of the released JPEG image. Calibrated with field stars, the RAW data show that the lens vignetting and the variation of the pixel solid angle reduce the signal of diffuse light by up to $\sim$70% at the edge of the field, and that the signal on the dark side of the Moon is most likely foreground light rather than an instrumental offset. Between 10 degrees and 15 degrees elongation, the radial profiles of the F-corona follow power laws with indices of $-2.0$ to $-2.3$ (east), $-2.5$ (west), and $-2.4$ to $-2.7$ (north and south), consistent with space-based observations, and the surface brightness along the ecliptic is $\sim$26 MJy sr$^{-1}$ ($\pm 7\%$) at 10 degrees. The isophotes have flattening indices of $\sim$0.6-0.7 and superellipse indices of $\sim$1.5-1.6. Comparison with the ZodiSURF zodiacal light model supports a radial dust density index of $α\simeq 1.3$ down to $\sim$0.2 au and suggests that the vertical distribution of the dust broadens toward the Sun. The JPEG image retains nearly the full vignetting, despite its metadata, and its tone response is not a single power law; together with the zero-point treatment, these effects account for the steep and asymmetric profiles reported previously, while the flattened morphology and $α\simeq 1.3$ are confirmed. We identify quantities robust in JPEG images and show that the tone response can be reconstructed from field stars.

title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds
abstract: Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances. Existing evaluations of social agents mainly rely on LLM judges that rate the conversation, without checking the resulting plan. We introduce HICO-Bench, a benchmark of 180 everyday coordination scenarios, such as resource allocation, scheduling, and authorization, in which two agents with private information converse and then independently record the plan they agreed on. A program checks Feasibility (the two records match and satisfy both participants' private conditions), and an LLM judge checks Integrity (the conversation supports the recorded plan); passing both is a Verified Success. Each scenario has two versions that share the same public context but differ in one private condition, so the correct plan differs between them. Across thirteen LLMs, 36% of conversations rated highly for goal completion fail Verified Success. To learn from outcomes that arrive only at the end of a conversation, we propose Paired-Credit Policy Optimization (PaCPO). After each turn, PaCPO asks the agent for a tentative plan, checks it in both versions of the scenario, and rewards the turns after which the tentative plans fit their respective versions. PaCPO raises Qwen3-8B's Verified Success from 20.4% to 28.3%.

title: Sensing-Aided Vehicular Beam Tracking: System Gain Over Link Feedback and Probe-Verified Sensing Invocation
abstract: Sensor-based beam prediction is usually evaluated against exhaustive beam training, leaving open when sensing adds useful information beyond a deployed tracker's link feedback and when it should be withheld. We separate system gain from the marginal value of sensing in action-restricted causal replay of recorded 64-beam sweeps from four vehicular DeepSense 6G scenarios. The replay exposes only serving-beam and explicitly probed candidate powers and counts probes and model invocations separately. The proposed controller combines a scheduled post-setup re-sweep with probe-verified sensing admission and blacklist backoff. In three scenarios where feedback-only tracking is within 0.25 dB of the recorded-sweep oracle, the controller stays close to feedback-only in mean loss while rarely invoking the model, whereas always-on sensing performs worse. In the sole high-innovation scenario, the controller's system gain is 0.82 dB (95% confidence interval [0.30, 1.40]) over the plain feedback-only tracker and 0.15 dB over a probe-limited re-sweeping reference, with fewer probes than either. Sensing and the re-sweep both correct setup lock loss. At the native decision interval, enabling sensing in the same controller yields no statistically resolved loss reduction but cuts probing by 21%. In this scenario, accurate sensing reduces loss relative to the sensor-disabled controller under emulated link noise, staleness or longer decision intervals. Weak or delayed sensing can instead increase loss despite probe verification. These exploratory results characterize sensing as a conditional substitute for RF probing or a source of loss reduction, depending on the limitations of link feedback and on the accuracy and timeliness of sensing.

title: Topological obstruction for Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$
abstract: We establish new restrictions on the virtual cohomological dimension of word hyperbolic groups admitting Anosov representations into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ ($p > q \geq 2$) or the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$. Our main result states that, if $P_k$ is the parabolic subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ stabilizing an isotropic $k$-plane in $\mathbb{R}^{p, q}$, a group admitting a $\{P_1,P_q\}$-Anosov representation into $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $p$. As a result, a $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$-convex cocompact subgroup of $\operatorname{PO}(p, q)$ cannot act properly discontinuously and cocompactly on $\mathbf{H}^{p, q-1}$. The main theorem also implies that a group admitting a $P_α$-Anosov representation into the exceptional Lie group $\operatorname{G}_2'$ has virtual cohomological dimension strictly less than $4$, where $α$ is a short restricted root of $\operatorname{G}_2'$. As an application, we prove that the homogeneous space $\operatorname{G}_2'/ \operatorname{SU}(2, 1)$ does not admit any compact quotient.

title: Geometric-resource bounds and permutation-averaged success probabilities for the WZP algorithm
abstract: Solving linear systems of equations is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. In this work, we extend the original WZP algorithm from real symmetric linear systems to complex Hermitian linear systems. We then study the success probability of the modified WZP algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. By expressing the postselection success probability as the expectation value of a positive operator, we derive upper and lower bounds of the maximal success probability over separable, incoherent, and real pure states. These bounds further establish connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity. We further show that, under permutation averaging, the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction, with its dependence determined by the alignment between the success operator and the equal-superposition state. We also investigate the preprocessed WZP algorithm under subgroup-constrained preprocessing. For the two-level family, the optimal success probability is determined by the maximal projection weight onto the orbit of the target projector. Our results provide a unified perspective on the WZP success probability under different operational constraints.

title: Scalar Laplace-Beltrami harmonics and curvature-induced radial mode mixing in Friedmann-like cosmologies
abstract: We develop a harmonic framework for spherically symmetric Friedmann-like geometries with constant scalar curvature but non-zero trace-free Ricci curvature. This preserves Friedmann-type isotropic expansion while introducing a radially varying tidal field and supporting anisotropic stress. We formulate the scalar Laplace-Beltrami operator as a Sturm-Liouville problem and establish its self-adjoint domains and regularity at minimal spheres. Robertson-Walker harmonics are recovered in the maximally symmetric limit. Trace-free curvature terms are expressed as spectral projection kernels. Rotational symmetry preserves angular labels and parity, while the tidal profile couples different radial eigenmodes. A finite-shell calculation displays this off-diagonal structure, verifies consistency between radial representations, and confirms the expected weak-field scaling. A minimally coupled scalar field remains diagonal in the exact basis, indicating operator-dependent mixing rather than mixing solely due to inhomogeneity. We formulate transverse-traceless kernels, whose dynamical application requires a specified model for the supporting anisotropic matter. This converts curvature-induced mode mixing into a spectral problem for perturbations beyond maximally symmetric cosmologies.

title: Drivers of LLM Consensus Formation Under Competing Incentives: A Simulation Study
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent environments that produce unanimous agreement, both in intended interactions that need coordination and in unintended emergent interactions. Consequently, understanding how LLMs with competing incentives reach consensus is crucial to better interpret and design LLM collectives. We introduce an evaluation, based on the Network Consensus game, to assess the mechanisms driving this process. Here, a network of agents must agree on one of two colours to receive a payoff, but agents are offered different payoffs for the agreed colour. We vary components such as communication access and network structure and assess six open-source models and one closed model (ChatGPT 5.6-sol). We find that open-source LLMs reach consensus less often than humans in comparable experiments and only if messages are communicated across the global network. ChatGPT 5.6-sol, however, is able to reach consensus with communication limited to its neighbours and with no communication ability. This is achieved through lower stubbornness and higher majority-following tendencies, and by providing more information about its neighbours' states in messages. However, situating agents in a highly clustered graph reduces consensus, regardless of these traits, demonstrating that both system design and individual model traits drive collective outcomes.

title: Biases in Ringdown Tests of General Relativity from Gravitational-Wave Microlensing
abstract: Gravitational-wave (GW) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (GR) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the Kerr hypothesis. However, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. We investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. We perform complementary time-domain post-merger and frequency-domain full inspiral--merger--ringdown analyses using unlensed waveform models. We find that lensing in the wave-optics regime can produce substantial biases in the inferred remnant mass and spin and can strongly affect the inferred modal content of the ringdown. In particular, it can spuriously favor the presence of the first overtone, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{221}_{220}\sim40$, even though the injected signal has no support for it. Parameterized ringdown tests can likewise yield strong apparent support for deviations from the Kerr quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm modGR}_{\rm GR}\sim8$. In contrast, the evidence for higher-order modes remains largely unchanged for the simulated signals considered here. The parameterized analysis using the entire signal further shows that microlensing can bias the inferred frequency of the dominant $(2,2,0)$ QNM. These results demonstrate that unmodeled microlensing can produce systematic biases and spurious signatures in ringdown analyses, potentially affecting precision tests of the Kerr hypothesis.

title: A hybrid quantum interferometer bridging Hong-Ou-Mandel and N00N-state interference
abstract: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference offers robustness in high-noise environments due to its phase-insensitive nature, while N00N-state interference provides enhanced phase sensitivity for precision measurements in low-noise settings. However, their realizations have typically required separate experimental platforms. Here, we report a single hybrid quantum interferometer that can dynamically transition between HOM and N00N-state interference by adjusting two time delays, $τ_1$ and $τ_2$. This tunability enables operation in phase-insensitive, phase-sensitive, or hybrid modes within a unified setup, as confirmed by theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration. Our system offers a versatile platform with potential for quantum sensing applications, paving the way for integrated quantum technologies capable of adapting to diverse noise conditions.

title: Investigating Behavior Cloning from Few Demonstrations for Autonomous Driving based on Bird's-Eye View in Simulated Cities
abstract: This paper investigates the use of Behavior Cloning (BC) for autonomous driving from a bird's-eye view (BEV) perspective in simulated urban environments. BC uses supervised learning to mimic expert driving behaviors. Previous works have applied BC in the CARLA simulator but did not fully address the challenges of traffic light compliance. Our approach enhances BC by integrating a kernel density estimator to adjust training sample weights based on action density, thereby improving the learning of rare but critical actions such as stopping at red lights and accelerating at green lights, specially in scenarios of scarce number of expert demonstrations. Using BEV inputs, which provide an abstract top-down view of the driving environment, our method simplifies the policy learning process. The trained convolutional neural network (CNN) outputs steering and acceleration actions based on these BEV inputs and additional state variables. Experimental results in the CARLA simulator demonstrate that our weighted BC method significantly improves driving performance, achieving higher route completion compared to standard BC. This weighted approach proved to be crucial in learning correct driving behaviors, particularly in test environments not encountered during training, highlighting its potential for enhancing autonomous vehicle navigation.

title: Learning to reconstruct Germano Differential Filtered Fields with Convolutional Neural Networks for Large Eddy Simulation of Plasma Turbulence
abstract: We present a novel method which combines the invertibility of the differential filter of Germano, with convolutional networks to accelerate plasma turbulence simulations. Rather than learning the mapping from coarse-grid LES fields to fine-grid DNS, the proposed method learns the mapping from coarse LES fields to the differential-filtered DNS fields. We then use the inverse of Germano's filter to reconstruct the fine-scale details and hence calculate exactly the nonlinear terms in the governing equations and subgrid-scale terms in the LES equations. The method is tested on the 2D Hasegawa-Wakatani (HW) and modified Hasegawa-Wakatani (mHW) plasma turbulence models at $256^2$ and $512^2$ DNS resolutions using 2, 4 and 8 times smaller LES grids in each direction. We compare the model with DNS results on energy, enstrophy, spectra, probability distributions, poloidal and radial fluxes and computational cost. Validation extends to 1000 simulation time units for HW and 100 for mHW, whose faster dynamics lead toward laminarization. For the $256^2$ cases, the finer LES meshes preserve several integral and spectral features, whereas the coarsest mesh yields unphysical behavior. In contrast, for the $512^2$ cases, even the coarsest LES mesh preserves the turbulent character of the flow and maintains acceptable statistics for both the HW and mHW models. Moreover, we show how our methodology is superior to traditional algebraic numerical LES models, which traditionally fail to capture important design features. Finally, benchmarks show an MPI task-time reductions of 4.82--49.45, with a maximum wall-clock speedup of $1.55\times$ when compared to full CPU socket.

title: What and Where in Identifying and Quantifying Conventions in Humans and AI Agents
abstract: Cooperative success rests in part on implicit communication. Partners converge on conventions: regularities that give an action meaning beyond its direct effect. Yet conventions are usually observed only indirectly: a score drop when partners are swapped shows that a convention existed, but not what it was or where it was used. In the card game Hanabi, the exact probability that a play fails can be computed from the hints received and the cards in view. Players who use conventions succeed more often than this prediction allows; the resulting margin is the convention gap. Off-belief learning provides a hierarchy of agents (levels 1-5) whose first level uses no conventions by construction and whose later levels use progressively more. For humans and these agents on one scale, we ask what the conventions are and where they are used. On what: in two independently collected corpora of human games, humans show a larger gap than every agent level. On the conventions both populations use, however, humans do no better than level 2. The human advantage is concentrated in a situation that no agent level learns to use: hints that point to a card other than the ones they touch. On where: conventions depend on what the player already knows about the card, not on how recently it was hinted, and they are used most in the mid-game; humans use them earlier and later in the game than the agents. In interventions on the agents, blocking a single high-gap situation costs little, because meaning reroutes to other situations, but blocking several together costs far more than the sum of the single costs. Thus, the convention gap turns conventions from an inferred cause of score loss into a measurable, comparable, and causally testable object.

title: Fast spectral methods for Volterra integral equations
abstract: We develop novel methods for the fast construction of spectral approximations to smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra integral operators and for the fast evaluation of smooth nonlinear Volterra integrals. The proposed methods employ the Duffy mapping, which transforms the original indefinite integral into a definite integral and maps the original causal triangular domain to a square, thereby avoiding any artificial extension of the kernel function. For smooth linear and weakly singular Volterra operators, the resulting approximations are almost-banded and lower-banded, respectively. The $N\times N$ principal finite section of these approximations can be constructed in $O(N)$ and $O(N^2)$ flops, respectively, via recurrence relations. For Volterra integrals with a smooth kernel that depends nonlinearly on a given function, recurrence relations lead to fast evaluation with a complexity of $O(N^2\log N)$ when the function is approximated by a degree-$N$ Chebyshev approximant. These spectral approximations and evaluation procedures give rise to fast and stable spectral methods for solving Volterra integral equations, as well as a broad class of problems involving Volterra integral operators. Extensive numerical experiments show that these spectral methods significantly outperform existing methods in terms of stability, speed, accuracy, and ease of implementation.

title: Characterization of $C^{1,α}$-domains in terms of Carleson-type $\varepsilon$-coefficients
abstract: Let $Ω=Ω^+\subset \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ be a bounded open set with $n$-Ahlfors regular boundary and let $Ω^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus\overline{Ω^+}$. For $x\in\partialΩ$, $r>0$, define \begin{equation*} \varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r):=\frac{1}{r^n} \inf_{H^+}\mathcal{H}^n\left(((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^+)\setminus Ω^+) \cup ((\partial B(x,r)\cap H^-)\setminus Ω^-)\right), \end{equation*} where $\mathcal{H}^n$ stands for $n$-dimensional Hausdorff measure and the infimum is taken over all open affine half-spaces $H^+$ such that $x\in \partial H^+$. Here $H^-=\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\setminus \overline{H^+}$. In this work we prove that $Ω$ is a $C^{1,α}$ open set, with $0<α<1$, if and only if there exists some constant $C>0$ such that $\varepsilon_{n,Ω}(x,r)\leq C\,r^α$ for all $x\in\partialΩ$ and all $0<r\leq \mathrm{diam}(\partialΩ)$.

title: Uniform non-homogeneous vector bundles: A counterexample to the conjecture of Drézet and Ballico-Ellia
abstract: We construct a rank-9 uniform non-homogeneous vector bundle on ${\mathbb P}^5$. This yields the first counterexample to the longstanding open conjecture that every uniform vector bundle of rank $r<2n$ on ${\mathbb P}^n$ is homogeneous.

title: HGRP: Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network for Routability Prediction
abstract: Routability prediction enables rapid evaluation of placement quality without routing, providing effective feedback for routability-driven placement optimization. Recent machine learning methods have achieved efficient routability prediction through data-driven approach. However, their prediction performance highly depends on the capability of input representations to capture essential circuit information. To address the limitations of existing circuit representations in simultaneously preserving logical topology, physical layout and routing resource information, this paper proposes HGRP, a heterogeneous graph neural network for routability prediction. HGRP models the cells, nets, and routing grids as distinct types of nodes and explicitly represents topological connectivity, spatial mapping, and grid adjacency, thereby constructing a heterogeneous graph representation that preserves multi-level circuit semantics. Based on the representation, a heterogeneous message passing mechanism is developed to enable information interaction and feature fusion among distinct types of nodes, effectively learning the complex correlations between circuit structures and routing behaviors. Experimental results on the CircuitNet dataset show that HGRP improves F1-score by 18.69\% relative improvements compared with the state-of-the-art in the congestion prediction task. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/ShenShan123/HGPR.

title: Robust Counterfactuals for Markov Decision Processes under Statistical and Causal Uncertainties
abstract: Counterfactual reasoning (asking what would have happened, had a decision been different) is a powerful tool for identifying causes of failure and explaining the behaviour of AI systems in sequential decision-making tasks. In Markov Decision Processes (MDPs), two sources of uncertainty complicate counterfactual inference: statistical uncertainty in the MDP transitions when the MDP is estimated from trajectory data, and uncertainty about the unknown causal model, as there are multiple structural causal models (SCMs) compatible with each MDP. Existing work addresses these two challenges in isolation. We address both simultaneously by introducing a framework for partial counterfactual inference in MDPs that is robust to both statistical and causal uncertainty. Our approach provides: 1) closed-form analytical bounds for the counterfactual probabilities that are valid across all SCMs entailed by a given interval MDP (IMDP); 2) a method to compute minimal robust interventions to achieve a desired counterfactual outcome via pessimistic value iteration on the induced counterfactual IMDP. Since the latter is constructed using our analytical bounds, our approach remains efficient and scalable to realistic MDP environments. Experiments across multiple case studies demonstrate our method's robustness and practical utility for identifying minimal sets of actions that, if changed, would have led to improved outcomes.

title: High-Frequency Mass Transfer Enabling Over-Limiting Currents in Porous Electrodes
abstract: Classical film theory predicts a finite diffusion-limited current at porous electrodes. However, over-limiting currents (OLCs), which exceed this limit, are often observed and have been attributed to surface charge, confinement, or electrokinetic effects. Here, we use a frequency-domain framework to identify a different mechanism governed by the time scale of concentration variation. For perfectly reactive interfaces, the spectral Sherwood number, a frequency-dependent dimensionless measure of interfacial mass transfer relative to molecular diffusion, grows as $\Shnd\simω^{1/2}$ at high frequency, while its phase approaches $π/4$. This response corresponds to the semi-infinite Warburg limit of the electrochemical impedance. A scaling analysis shows that the exponent and prefactor are determined by diffusion within a thin layer adjacent to the interface and are therefore independent of the global pore geometry. Numerical results for parallel plates, circular tubes, and twelve porous microstructures confirm this scaling. Geometry, flow strength, and flow direction affect the low-frequency response and crossover frequency, but not the asymptotic scaling in the high-frequency limit. This temporal route to OLCs requires neither surface charge nor confinement and could inform the design of systems for pulsed electrodeposition, mineral recovery and renewable-energy storage.

title: $χ$-Independence for BPS Invariants of Warped Local Curves
abstract: A well-known conjecture of Toda's asserts that the BPS invariants associated to a Calabi--Yau threefold are independent of the chosen Euler characteristic. We answer the question in the affirmative for a certain class of local surfaces, which we call warped local curves. Along the way we show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a warped local curve can be written as the global critical locus of a function. We also show that the moduli stack of sheaves on a curve fibration over $\mathbb{A}^1$ is the global critical locus of a function.

title: Stable atomic vector bundles are 1-obstructed
abstract: We prove that every stable atomic (twisted) vector bundle on a projective hyper-Kähler manifold is 1-obstructed. In the appendix, we construct a simple atomic object that is not 1-obstructed, providing a counterexample to Beckmann's conjecture.

title: Genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields
abstract: We define genus character $L$-functions of orders in quadratic function fields of odd characteristic. We express each as a product of two quadratic $L$-functions and explicit local factors at primes dividing the conductor, with a possible shift of the variable in one of the two quadratic $L$-functions. This product formula yields meromorphic continuation and functional equations. In the real case, we evaluate special values in terms of continued fractions and derive formulas for the product of class numbers of two imaginary quadratic function fields. These formulas are function field analogues of the Kaneko-Mizuno-Zagier formula.

title: Wearable Data Profiling for NDN-Based Smart Healthcare: Performance Comparison with an IP Baseline
abstract: Smart healthcare IoT requires low-latency and reliable delivery of patient data, yet IP-based communication remains host-centric and offers limited support for mobility, caching, and request aggregation. This paper evaluates a smartphone-centric Named Data Networking (NDN) approach in which a patient's smartphone aggregates sensor streams and publishes a stable latest profile under a consistent name, enabling effective in-network caching. Using ndnSIM simulations on a realistic medical IoT topology, we compare NDN and IP under identical traffic and link conditions. Results show that per-sample naming provides little benefit, but smartphone aggregation with stable naming allows NDN caching to reduce delay after cache warm-up and achieve significantly higher delivery ratios under congestion compared to IP.

title: A Topological\-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for Scalable and Interpretable Modeling of Two\-Dimensional Carbon Networks
abstract: We introduce a compact Topological-Geometrical Descriptor (TGD) for planar two-dimensional carbon networks. Atomic coordinates are mapped to a periodic planar graph and represented through ring populations, topological-charge statistics, projected ring geometry, and dual-graph defect adjacency. The resulting modeling vector contains 19 physically interpretable features. We evaluate TGD on 120 published planar carbon allotropes using the DFT relative energy per atom with respect to graphene as the target. Repeated five-fold cross-validation with gradient boosting yields a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.0826 +/- 0.0138 eV/atom and R2 = 0.803 +/- 0.074. Under the same validation protocol, TGD gives a mean MAE of 0.0828 eV/atom, compared with 0.0929 eV/atom for a 203-feature Matminer representation. We further analyze 360 vacancy-defected graphene configurations spanning 12 vacancy concentrations from 2 to 24 percent. When entire vacancy concentrations are held out, TGD gives a pooled MAE of 0.269 eV/vacancy and R2 = 0.861, outperforming simple baselines based on vacancy concentration alone or non-hexagonal-ring fraction alone. Sensitivity tests show that the inferred edge sets are stable to moderate changes in the adaptive bond factor. Finally, the mean absolute topological charge is examined as a one-variable empirical surrogate for the allotrope dataset and is treated explicitly as dataset-specific rather than universal. These results show that TGD combines compact prediction with direct structural interpretation while making clear the present restriction to single-layer planar carbon networks.

title: Continual pretraining Prostate MRI ViT Encoder for task alignment
abstract: Building foundation models for MRI has emerged as a promising direction for advancing medical image analysis and improving accessibility of task specific models. Existing approaches primarily focus on effective pretraining strategies and evaluating their performance across diverse downstream tasks. While these methods show performance gains, limited attention has been given to understanding task alignment between pretraining and downstream objectives. Unlike language models, where the two stages are naturally aligned, such alignment is less evident in vision based applications. Motivated by this gap, we explore continual pretraining. Specifically, continually pretraining a pretrained ViT encoder using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) on a prostate segmentation task to enhance task alignment and downstream performance. We further perform layer-wise representational analysis using Centered Kernel Alignment (CKA) to assess representational shifts and their correlation with task outcomes. Our experiments show improved performance in 3 of 6 downstream tasks and comparable results in the others. Our Feature analysis reveals that, for segmentation tasks, continually pretrained encoder features exhibit greater similarity to those of the finetuned encoder than the original pretrained encoder, correlating with observed performance gains.

title: Mixed Poisson diffusion models and application to posterior sampling
abstract: Diffusion models are a powerful framework for learning complex probability distributions. While widely used diffusion models for continuous data rely on Gaussian noising processes, we instead develop diffusion models based on Poisson noise. More precisely, we introduce and study a new mathematical framework, called Mixed Poisson Diffusion Models (MPDM), with noising dynamics driven by multivariate counting processes. Our methodology is motivated by Poisson inverse problems. The success of Gaussian diffusion models has led to their use as prior models in a growing number of posterior sampling methods for inverse problems. However, most of these approaches focus on Gaussian inverse problems, in which observations are generated through a deterministic forward operator corrupted by additive Gaussian noise. By contrast, Poisson inverse problems, where observations are discrete and Poisson distributed, remain comparatively underexplored in this literature. Building on our Poisson generative dynamics, we develop a natural framework for posterior sampling in Poisson inverse problems and derive several posterior sampling algorithms based on the proposed model. We evaluate our approach on realistic Poisson inverse problems and show that the resulting framework is well suited to this class of problems.

title: TRP-UE Bistatic Sensing for 6G Performance Analysis and Insights
abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) equips cellular networks with the dual capability of data transmission and environmental sensing by sharing spectrum, waveforms, and radio hardware. While network-side sensing via transmission-reception points (TRPs) has been widely investigated, the use of user equipment (UEs) as sensing receivers introduces additional bistatic viewpoints and can improve target observability. UE-assisted operation is nevertheless constrained by small UE apertures and by waveform processing, especially when data-bearing communication signals are reused for sensing. The present paper investigates theoretical limits and operating conditions for UE-assisted passive target positioning, with emphasis on hybrid operation that fuses TRP--TRP and TRP--UE measurements. A unified OFDM-based signal-and-noise model is developed to cover both positioning reference signals (PRS) and communication waveform reuse with modulation-dependent noise enhancement. Based on this model, closed-form Fisher-information expressions and Cramer-Rao lower bounds are derived for delay and angular parameters and are mapped to positioning error bounds (PEBs) for two estimator classes: time-angle positioning based on TDOA + DoA and delay-only 3D ellipsoid positioning based on excess-delay/TDOA measurements. Monte-Carlo simulations across reference SNR, subcarrier spacing and occupied bandwidth, modulation order, radar cross section (RCS), sensing mode, and positioning algorithm identify regimes where UE participation and hybrid sensing provide significant gains and quantify the associated estimator-to-bound trade-offs.

title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
abstract: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models. Today's dominant approach distills a bidirectional diffusion model into a causal few-step student, but existing pipelines make this conversion prohibitively expensive, requiring offline Probability Flow ODE} (PF-ODE) trajectories that cost tens of thousands of GPU-hours and terabytes of storage. We show it can be made dramatically more efficient. Pushing this efficiency to its extreme, we reduce trajectory supervision to a single sample, the strictest setting possible, and find that it causes severe quality collapse. We trace this to the teacher's trajectory geometry: the high-noise regime, governing semantic layout and motion, and the low-noise regime, governing fine texture exhibit fundamentally different curvature and optimization behavior, so a single monolithic student cannot jointly fit both, causing severe representation interference. Motivated by this, we propose Glance Forcing, a lightweight distillation framework that decouples the denoising trajectory into two complementary slow and fast experts, each guided by a tailored, stage-specific objective, while keeping the pretrained teacher entirely frozen. This decoupling further reveals a general mechanism underlying few-step distillation: PF-ODE distillation mainly straightens the few-step trajectory geometry, while the subsequent distribution-matching stage independently governs distributional quality. Using only one PF-ODE trajectory, Glance Forcing already surpasses the fully-trained state-of-the-art baseline, raising the VBench Total score from 84.04 to 84.22 while cutting trajectory-collection cost from thousands of GPU-hours to about one A100-GPU-hour, with markedly larger gains in dynamic degree, VisionReward, and instruction-following, and consistent preference from human raters over strong baselines.

title: Scaling Multilingual Safety and Reasoning Evaluation through Reasoning-Guided Translation
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed across languages, yet their safety and reasoning capabilities remain predominantly evaluated in English. Translating existing benchmarks offers a scalable approach to multilingual evaluation, but preserving task-specific meaning across languages presents significant challenges, particularly for harmful requests, mathematical reasoning, and conversational interactions. We introduce a reasoning-guided translation framework for constructing multilingual evaluations designed to preserve the structure and intended meaning of diverse benchmark tasks. Our approach separates translation strategy selection from large-scale generation, combining reasoning-guided configuration selection with task-aware validation, targeted repair, and independent quality screening. Using this framework, we develop a source-aligned evaluation collection spanning seven safety, conversational, and mathematical reasoning resources across 11 languages. The resulting collection achieves 99.94\% coverage of intended item--language pairs in the two subsets requiring repair. Evaluations of open-source LLMs reveal distinct language-dependent vulnerabilities, including inconsistent refusal behaviour and substantial reasoning degradation in lower-resource languages. These findings highlight the importance of task-sensitive benchmark construction and systematic quality assessment for understanding multilingual model behaviour beyond English.

title: A Multiarmed Bandit Approach for LTE-U/Wi-Fi Coexistence in a Multicell Scenario
abstract: Recent studies and literature reviews have shown promising results for 3GPP system solutions in unlicensed bands when coexisting with Wi-Fi, either by using the duty cycle (DC) approach or licensed-assisted access (LAA). However, it is widely known that general performance in these coexistence scenarios is dependent on traffic and how the duty cycle is adjusted. Most DC solutions configure their parameters statically, which can result in performance losses when the scenario experiences changes on the offered data. In our previous works, we demonstrated that reinforcement learning (RL) techniques can be used to adjust DC parameters. We showed that a Q-learning (QL) solution that adapts the LTE DC ratio to the transmitted data rate can maximize the Wi-Fi/LTE-Unlicensed (LTE-U) aggregated throughput. In this paper, we extend our previous solution by implementing a simpler and more efficient algorithm based on multiarmed bandit (MAB) theory. We evaluate its performance and compare it with the previous one in different traffic scenarios. The results demonstrate that our new solution offers improved balance in throughput, providing similar results for LTE and Wi-Fi, while still showing a substantial system gain. Moreover, in one of the scenarios, our solution outperforms the previous approach by 6% in system throughput. In terms of user throughput, it achieves more than 100% gain for the users at the 10th percentile of performance, while the old solution only achieves a 10% gain.

title: ObjDream: Guiding Vision-Language-Action Models with Object-Level Understanding and Future State Prediction
abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have emerged as a powerful paradigm for robotic manipulation, enabling robots to generate actions from visual observations and language instructions. However, most existing VLA models still operate on image-level visual representations inherited from pretrained vision-language backbones, while lacking fine-grained object understanding for manipulation. As a result, their robustness can degrade under out-of-distribution object layouts, clutter, and background variations. To address these limitations, we introduce ObjDream, an object-centric VLA framework centered on object-level understanding and future object state prediction. ObjDream uses a spatio-temporal object encoder to organize visual observations into temporal object slots, where persistent object identity and dynamic object state are represented through separate channels. These structured object representations are inserted into the token sequence of the vision-language model (VLM), where identity-guided routing modulates VLM attention to the corresponding object tokens. In addition, an action-conditioned object dynamics module predicts compact future object states relevant to manipulation during training, explicitly supervising object state evolution under robot actions without requiring future prediction at inference. Experiments on LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and RoboTwin 2.0 show that ObjDream improves generalization under diverse distribution shifts and scene perturbations. Real-world robot experiments further demonstrate that ObjDream transfers to physical manipulation settings with novel object arrangements and background changes.

title: Design Space Exploration of Reinforcement Learning Configurations for Post-Legalization Placement
abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Reinforcement Learning (RL) have recently been explored for VLSI placement optimization, but their effectiveness for post-legalization placement refinement remains unclear. This paper presents a systematic design space exploration of a GNN-Proximal Policy Optimization (GNN-PPO) framework across three ISPD2015 benchmarks. We evaluate 18 configurations covering reward functions, GNN architectures, action spaces, candidate-set sizes, and training strategies. We analyse the results we obtain to identify pitfalls and to assess the prospects and opportunities of the RL methods for post-legalization placement. On top of that we propose a design classification approach to guide the design decisions of RL models.

title: Asymptotic Error Distributions for Euler-Maruyama Schemes with Additive Semimartingale Noise
abstract: We establish a joint stable limit theorem for integrated discretization errors of finite-dimensional càdlàg semimartingales whose predictable characteristics are absolutely continuous in time and satisfy a pathwise integrability condition. The normalized integrated error, evaluated on the discretization grid, converges stably jointly with the discretized semimartingale in the vector-valued Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. No martingale representation property is assumed. We apply this theorem to the Euler-Maruyama scheme for stochastic differential equations with additive semimartingale noise. For a $C^1$ drift with locally Lipschitz derivative and a nonexplosive solution, the grid-point error normalized by $n$ converges stably jointly with the discretized driver. The limiting error solves a linear integral equation with an explicit inhomogeneous term involving the driver, an auxiliary Brownian motion, and independent uniform marks attached to the jumps. We also obtain the same limit under two alternative drift regularity conditions based on small-jump integrability or Lévy semigroup smoothing. For continuous drivers, the continuous-time error converges stably in the uniform topology.

title: Smart Fusion for Adaptive Visual-IMU Weighting in cuVSLAM Sparse Bundle Adjustment
abstract: In cuVSLAM, visual and inertial measurement unit (IMU) residuals are fused in sparse bundle adjustment (SBA) with a weighting fixed by pre-calibrated noise covariances, leaving no mechanism to adapt the visual-inertial balance at runtime. We introduce a scalar $α\geq1$ that upscales the visual information matrix relative to the IMU preintegration constraint. Across the candidate set $\{1.0,2.0,5.0,10.0,20.0\}$, the resulting trajectories form two empirical performance regimes. The IMU-TRUST regime contains $α\in\{1,2\}$ near the calibrated baseline, while the VISION-TRUST regime contains $α\in\{10,20\}$. The intermediate value $α=5$ is treated as a transition case. Differences within each regime are small relative to those observed between the regimes. This structure motivates reducing $α$-selection to a binary decision. We train a lightweight Visual Quality Estimator (VQE), implemented as a multilayer perceptron with 914 trainable parameters. It maps a 10-dimensional visual quality feature vector assembled from statistics already maintained by the tracker to a per-SBA regime prediction. The proposed method reduces mean RMSE APE by $27.7\%$ and by $14.9\%$ under leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) on EuRoC MAV and TUM-VI Room, respectively.

title: Let Me Clarify: Interactive Modeling of Soft Attributes
abstract: People commonly express preferences through soft attributes such as is interesting,'' which are difficult to operationalize for computational preference modeling. Latent representations can obscure how such attributes are interpreted, limiting transparency and user control. We formalize softness as the diversity of valid interpretations a description permits and provide empirical support for this characterization. Our proposed measure estimates softness to guide clarification and determine when to generate computational approximations. This is instantiated in AttriFy, a mixed-initiative system that translates descriptions into executable Python functions over text corpora. An interactive dashboard connects the dialogue to proposed functions and computed values, enabling users to inspect, accept, reject, and refine interpretations. An exploratory within-subjects study with 32 participants compares our softness-guided clarification approach with an LLM baseline in supporting interpretable attribute construction. This work positions softness as a basis for constructing explicit, user-steerable attribute dimensions for downstream preference elicitation and decision-making.

title: Spin and 3D structure: theoretical advances
abstract: Theoretical studies of hadron structure have made important progress since the previous DIS workshop in 2025. This talk reviews selected new results and developments, with a focus on spin dependent parton distributions, on transverse-momentum distributions and their rapidity dependence, on generalised parton distributions, and on the evaluation of power corrections.

title: The minimal width of neural networks and immersions of real projective space
abstract: We investigate the minimal width of deep neural networks that can approximate all continuous functions from $\mathbb{R}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^m$ in the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. We show that whenever the real projective space $\mathbb{RP}^{n-1}$ admits a smooth immersion into $\mathbb{R}^n$, the minimal width is at least $n+\min\{n,m\}$, assuming that the activation function is continuous and monotone. As a consequence, the minimal width of ReLU networks is $n+m$ whenever $n$ is equal to 2, 3, 4, 7 or 8 and $1\le m \le n$, extending results of Hanin-Sellke and Hwang. This suggests an intriguing connection between the approximation theory of neural networks and differential topology.

title: Multi-Cell LTE-U/Wi-Fi Coexistence Evaluation Using a Reinforcement Learning Framework
abstract: Cellular broadband Internet of Things (IoT) applications are expected to keep growing year-by-year, generating demands from high throughput services. Since some of these applications are deployed over licensed mobile networks, as long term evolution (LTE), one already common problem is faced: the scarcity of licensed spectrum to cope with the increasing demand for data rate. The LTE-Unlicensed (LTE-U) forum, aiming to tackle this problem, proposed LTE-U to operate in the 5 GHz unlicensed spectrum. However, Wi-Fi is already the consolidated technology operating in this portion of the spectrum, besides the fact that new technologies for unlicensed band need mechanisms to promote fair coexistence with the legacy ones. In this work, we extend the literature by analyzing a multi-cell LTE-U/Wi-Fi coexistence scenario, with a high interference profile and data rates targeting a cellular broadband IoT deployment. Then, we propose a centralized, coordinated reinforcement learning framework to improve LTE-U/Wi-Fi aggregate data rates. The added value of the proposed solution is assessed by a ns-3 simulator, showing improvements not only in the overall system data rate but also in average user data rate, even with the high interference of a multi-cell environment.

title: Exact map-space beam convolution via spin-mapmaking
abstract: Forthcoming cosmic microwave background (CMB) experiments are targeting ambitious science goals, including the exploration of the particle content of the Universe across cosmic times and the search for the faint signal from primordial gravitational waves. To pursue these goals, CMB experiments will house an unprecedented high number of detectors that will dramatically enhance their sensitivity. This will in turn require a tight control of instrumental systematics, demanding efficient and precise simulation of systematic effects. Leveraging spin-mapmaking, we present a map-based method to propagate beam convolution systematics to the map-level, especially well-suited for main-beam studies. From the scanning strategy information compressed into precomputed h-maps and the beam and sky harmonic coefficients, our method directly outputs beam convolved maps. We validate against pixel-centered TOD-level 4π convolution for circular, elliptical, and Planck HFI scanning beams, demonstrating that our method retains agreement to numerical precision, while operating in map space. This formalism enables efficient simulation of beam convolution systematics across the full focal plane of upcoming experiments. As a first practical application, we demonstrate the ability to efficiently produce beam-convolved simulated Planck maps, showing excellent agreement with the QuickPol pipeline at the power-spectrum level. We release a public code, Smarties4Planck, to easily generate such maps for broader use.

title: Invariant complex structures on the Euclidean motion group as deformations of Calabi-Eckmann structures
abstract: We classify, up to equivalence, all left-invariant complex structures on the three-dimensional Euclidean rigid motion group $SE(3).$ Our approach is based on the correspondence between complex structures on a real Lie algebra $\mathfrak{e}(3)$ of the motion group and complex Lie subalgebras of the complexification of $\mathfrak{e}(3).$ The resulting structures form a one-parameter family $J_ϕ.$ We further establish a connection with the classical Calabi-Eckmann complex structures on $S^3\times S^3.$ More precisely, we construct a one-parameter deformation of Lie brackets connecting $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus \mathfrak{so}(3)$ to $\mathfrak{e}(3),$ for which each endomorphism $J_ϕ$ remains integrable. Consequently, every left-invariant complex structure on $SE(3)$ arises as a contraction limit of Calabi-Eckmann structures. The same family of endomorphisms also defines complex structures on $\mathfrak{so}(3,1).$

title: Exact Cap Response and Aperture Selection for Molecular Communication under Aligned Drift
abstract: Spatial reception under directed molecule transport requires balancing useful molecule capture against intersymbol interference (ISI).
