Assume that there is no trapped surface in this region and assume that the Doppler exponent (blue shift) along each incoming null cone is uniformly bounded. We then prove that the solution can extend regularly across $\mathcal{O}$ provided the mass ratio $μ=2m/r$ satisfies $\supμ<\frac38$. This improves the small-mass-ratio condition in Christodoulou's extension principle by an explicit threshold of order one. Our proof has three new ingredients. First, we derive several new uniform scale-critical pointwise estimates for the scalar field and its derivatives. Second, we obtain refined estimates in an exterior self-similar domain within the triangular causal past region. Third, we establish a family of higher-order Morawetz-type identities and identify the ranges of $μ$, with which there are coercive spacetime estimates. The unweighted identity yields the threshold $μ\leq\frac14$, while employing extra self-similar weight raises the threshold to $μ<\frac38$ and provides a weighted control, which implies that the solution's BV norm along an outgoing null cone is small, so that Christodoulou's theory of bounded variation solutions gives the extension.

title: An extension principle for Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system with finite Doppler exponent
abstract: We prove a new extension principle for the spherically symmetric Einstein--Maxwell--charged scalar field system. Rather than imposing conditions for mass ratio $2m/r$ as in Christodoulou's small-mass-ratio criterion or as in An--Chen--Singh's proof [1] with $2m/r<3/8$, here we work through a proposal by An-Tan [2] with finite Doppler exponent (blueshift). By conducting two successive blow-up analyses, followed by a stationary comparison and a rigidity argument, we establish the uniform boundness of $α'$ with $α'=\partial_vα/\partial_vr$ and $α=\partial_v(rϕ)/\partial_vr$. This provides the desired extension principle in An-Tan [2] and completes the picture of weak cosmic censorship developed therein. As we were about to release our preprint, Cicortas communicated to us that together with his collaborators, they concomitantly used a different approach to obtain the corresponding extension principle with finite blueshift (Doppler exponent) for the uncharged Einstein-scalar field system. Hence, we decided to put the current paper as an appendix to An-Tan [2], thereby completing the proof of the weak cosmic censorship for the Einstein-Maxwell-charged scalar field system. At the same time, we are working with Cicortas and his collaborators to write a new preprint containing both approaches for the Einstein-scalar field system.

title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
abstract: Lab-scale membrane distillation (MD) modules are commonly used for membrane characterization and developing empirical heat-transfer correlations. Entrance-induced flow structures can introduce geometry-specific effects into measured temperature polarization (TP) and heat transfer. However, the dependence of these effects on module geometry and flow condition remains unclear. We performed three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of direct contact membrane distillation (DCMD) over inlet Reynolds numbers of $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}=10$-$1000$, focusing on side-chamber length and main-channel height. We discovered that counter-rotating streamwise vortices formed near the main-channel entrance across all geometries, but their downstream persistence increased with $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}$. At lower $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}$, the vortices mostly decayed before mid-channel, while at higher $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}$ they persisted farther downstream and produced pronounced spatial variations in TP. Increasing side-chamber length reduced the secondary-flow kinetic energy entering the main channel, and generally strengthened TP, whereas increasing main-channel height reduced the bulk velocity and streamwise kinetic energy, resulting in a thicker thermal boundary layer and stronger TP. For most geometries, the deviation from the straight-channel baseline changed from stronger TP at lower $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}$ to weaker TP at higher $\Re_{\mathrm{in}}$. Entrance effects therefore vary in both magnitude and direction with operating condition and cannot be represented by a constant correction across the Reynolds-number range.

title: Quantizer Redundancy and Exact Index Recoding in a Frozen Neural Audio Codec
abstract: Residual scalar quantization can produce highly dependent indices when successive stages reuse identical, unscaled grids. This case study examines that behavior in a frozen neural audio codec and develops an exact recoding procedure that reduces storage while preserving its decoder inputs. Analysis of the repeated-grid recurrence identifies predictable stage sequences; finite-precision checks motivate preserving every original index through explicit exception records. The model weights and reconstruction graph remain fixed. On the studied 62- and 512-file cohorts, a predictor, adaptive coding and explicit file selection reduce complete stored bytes. The final 512-file rate is 129.591 kbps including headers, 25.943% below an original-index XZ control. Original recorded CPU runs establish bitwise latent and waveform preservation; independent readers verify exact index and metadata recovery in subsequent saved-stream experiments. Later coding choices use previously studied cohorts, and fresh encoding requires generating three alternatives. The engineering result is implementation-specific storage reduction with exact index recovery; the underlying lossy reconstruction quality remains unchanged.

title: ChronoCulture: Evaluating Cultural Awareness Across Time in Large Language Models
abstract: Cultural attitudes and social norms evolve over time, yet most cultural benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) treat culture as a static attribute of a country or region. We introduce ChronoCulture, a benchmark of 10,360 temporal pairs built from longitudinal survey data across 72 countries. Each pair contains the same survey question asked in the same country in an older and a newer year, with full population response distributions as ground truth. Across six LLMs, we find that models can often predict a country's attitudes at one point in time but do not reliably capture how those attitudes change. Their predictions for different years tend to stay close together, failing to capture much of the observed change. Specifying the intended year in the prompt also offers little overall improvement in alignment with survey responses. These findings suggest that models often present a largely static picture of cultural attitudes, highlighting the need to evaluate cultural awareness across time.

title: SafeAdapt-Poker: Counterfactual Risk Calibration for Budgeted Adaptation under Opponent Shift
abstract: Opponent histories can mislead after behavioral shifts. SafeAdapt-Poker formulates budgeted adaptation under opponent shift as a dual-counterfactual sequential-control problem using only information available before each decision. At each decision the controller asks two distinct questions: what local downside a deviation from the frozen anchor would induce under matched legal continuations, and what future adaptation value would be lost by consuming part of the remaining deviation budget now. The first question is answered by a monotone strategic-risk model over deviation intensity; the second by a paired budget-state continuation model that prices current budget consumption. The controller selects among support-preserving candidate deviations by trading immediate adaptation value against these two quantities, a pathwise cumulative-KL ledger bounds total anchor-relative deviation, and a finite family of frozen controllers is screened on complete paired calibration sessions before held-out interaction. A finite-candidate perturbation bound shows that the allocation objective degrades continuously with continuation-value estimation error. Evaluation covers exact-game exploitation and safety, four opponent shifts, local-risk calibration, delayed-opportunity allocation, direct opportunity-value estimation, value-error robustness, factorial mechanism attribution, budget sensitivity, abstract-HUNL cross-play, and player/time-held-out public-history behavior. On exact Leduc the full controller attains a matched weak-pool gain of +0.0718 with a worst-opponent delta of -0.0126, raises delayed-opportunity capture from 0.6318 under myopic allocation to 0.7841 under the same session budget, and reaches +42.7 mbb/hand in abstract-HUNL cross-play; the retained public-history screen reports 0.5820 action accuracy and 0.9277 log loss versus 0.5039 and 0.9778 for a public prior.

title: AdaRSI: On-Demand Recursive Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
abstract: Pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) often fail midway through unseen long-horizon tasks. Recursive self-improvement (RSI) offers a remedy, but embodied RSI methods either refine the harness around a frozen executor and so cannot add a missing motion, or train the executor on persistent failures without asking whether a failure lies in how the executor is called or in what it can do. We ask when a self-improving embodied system should change the weights of its executor, and propose AdaRSI, an on-demand RSI framework for embodied agents. A coding agent first improves its skills and harness, then attributes persistent failures by retrying failing sub-steps from saved states, and fine-tunes only the sub-steps that remain unreliable, with demonstrations it collects itself and experience carried over from earlier tasks. On all 50 target tasks of RoboCasa365, with GR00T N1.5 as the executor and no human demonstrations, AdaRSI improves the VLA on all three suites and raises its success on unseen composite tasks from 4.6% to 13.8%. Compared with fine-tuning every sub-step, it reaches slightly higher success while using only 28% of the GPU time and 22% of the self-collected demonstrations, and fine-tuning without a harness trains more yet gains far less.

title: The contact frontier in Galactic civilization networks: radial structure and the Galactic habitable zone
abstract: The probability of interstellar contact depends not only on the abundance of technological civilizations but also on their spatial connectivity. Treating civilizations as nodes linked whenever their separation is smaller than the distance a signal travels within a communicative lifetime, we determine the radial structure of Galactic civilization networks. An exponential stellar disc replaces the uniform disc of earlier work, and the fraction of stars hosting civilizations may vary with radius as a Galactic Habitable Zone (GHZ). The isolation, contact and network transitions are frontiers several kiloparsecs wide, not boundaries: the contact frontier is set entirely by the disc scale length, and the network frontier, broadened by gradient percolation, stays near 1.5 scale lengths. The two frontiers overlap over a band containing the Sun, where both transitions proceed at once. Within this factorized GHZ model, the radius of peak civilization density depends only logarithmically on the strength of supernova sterilization, and the wide range of published peak radii, from the Galactic centre to 12 kpc, is reproduced primarily by varying that one parameter. Under the present normalization, the location of the zone has only a modest effect on the local contact probability, whereas the modelled Galactic connectivity is minimized when the civilization-density peak lies near the solar Galactocentric radius, where current determinations place the peak.

title: Tiered-Resolution Volumetric Mapping for Real-Time Simultaneous Planning and Mapping on Natural Outdoor Environments
abstract: Real-time volumetric mapping for a planning robot is dominated by the cost of integrating and storing information at the finest resolution, yet only a small fraction of any map ever lies on or near a path the planner actually considers. We exploit this with a tiered-resolution mapping mechanism that integrates LiDAR into a single map structure at two resolutions simultaneously: fine inside a corridor around the robot's current plan, and coarse everywhere else. As opposed to traditional navigation pipelines where path planning uses the mapping result and provides no feedback, we propose a feedback loop where planning also informs mapping to dynamically integrate information at different leaf resolutions. Across two real-world teleoperated datasets, replayed and scored offline against an independent full-resolution map, the tiered maps are 13-15x smaller and require 6-8x less integration CPU time than a uniform fine map, while producing paths at a similar cost per meter as the ones generated from fine resolution maps on both scenarios. A uniform coarse map reaches the same size savings but its path quality collapses (+210% cost per meter) on the harder scenario, because it over-discretizes terrain the robot must traverse. Tiering approximates the coarse map's cheapness without its failure mode.

title: LHAASO Constraints on New-Source Cosmic Rays:Abundance Scenarios and Injection Spectral Indices
abstract: Recent LHAASO observations indicate that microquasars and massive star clusters contribute to Galactic cosmic rays, and likely also to the pre-knee spectral hardening. Their markedly different astrophysical environments, compared with supernova remnants (SNRs), may imprint distinct cosmic-ray abundances. We investigate the spectra and composition of new-source cosmic rays under two abundance scenarios: Case-1, the SNR-like composition with enhanced heavy nuclei, and Case-2, the surface abundances of microquasar companion stars. We constrain injection spectral indices using LHAASO proton, helium, and all-particle spectra, and use their <lnA> data for model discrimination. Under the assumption of a unified heavy-element injection spectrum, Case-2 fits the <lnA> data significantly better than Case-1, but at the cost of large, physically unmotivated differences between heavy-element and He injection indices. This suggests the need to either relax the unified heavy-element injection-index assumption or explore alternative abundance patterns. We predict that if the new-source composition follows Case-1, the individual elemental spectral indices before the knee should remain nearly consistent; if it follows Case-2, the Mg, Si, and Fe spectra will be significantly softer than those of He, C, and O. Future element-resolved energy-spectrum measurements by HERD and LHAASO will provide a decisive test of this discriminating feature.

title: Crystallographic quotients of Artin braid groups and torus bundles over flat $3$-manifolds
abstract: For $n\geq3$, let $\overline B_n=B_n/[P_n,P_n]$ be the crystallographic quotient of the Artin braid group, with translation subgroup $\overline P_n=P_n/[P_n,P_n]\cong\mathbb Z^N$, where $N=\binom n2$. We prove that every compact connected flat $3$-manifold $M$, considered up to affine equivalence, is the base of a geometric torus bundle whose total space is a compact flat manifold with fundamental group a Bieberbach subgroup of some $\overline B_n$. More precisely, for every $n\geq n_M$, where $n_M\in\{3,4,5\}$ is an explicit optimal threshold depending on $M$, we construct a Bieberbach subgroup $Γ_n(M)\leq\overline B_n$ of dimension $N$ and a complete normal subgroup $K_n(M)\cong\mathbb Z^{N-3}$ consisting of translations such that $$ Γ_n(M)/K_n(M)\congπ_1(M). $$ We also determine which of the associated torus-bundle group extensions split: for the realizations constructed here, splitting occurs for exactly four of the ten affine-equivalence classes of compact flat $3$-manifolds.

title: Lost in Translation: Why Lower Bias Scores Don't Mean Fairer Models
abstract: Bias audits of multilingual language models usually compare a model's average stereotype score in English with its average in another language and read the difference as a difference in fairness. We ask how much of that difference is noise. Auditing ten open models in eight languages, we measure how far scores move when English test items are merely reworded, test every language shift item by item, and check that the test catches shifts we inject on purpose. In all 70 model-language pairs the stereotype score falls below its English level, and for Hindi, Korean and Swahili the drop clearly exceeds what rewording English produces; most of it comes from StereoSet items. Judging every translation, we find that imperfect ones drop more, but faithful translations alone drop nearly as much. Still, a lower average does not show that a model is fairer. An item's English score predicts its translated score far less well than its reworded score (correlation 0.23, 0.27 on faithful translations, vs. 0.48), while scores stay as far from neutral, models agree on translated items, and within Hindi or Spanish a translated item's score correlates with its own rewording at 0.84 and 0.82. The average cannot distinguish lower bias from a different pattern of item-level scores. We also document three common pipeline errors that silently erase bias signal, and release our code.

title: Transference principles for divergence sets of dispersive equations and their applications
abstract: In this article, we study the fractal refinement of the Carleson's problem: (1) We introduce an equivalence relation on linear dispersive PDEs on $\mathbb{R}^{n}$ based on the high-frequency oscillation of their Fourier multipliers, proving that equations in the same class share the same Hausdorff dimension of divergence sets. As applications, we estimate these dimensions for abstract dispersive families. Consequently, we recover known $1$-dimensional results for linearized Boussinesq and Beam propagations, while establishing new results for both in higher dimensions and for Klein-Gordon propagations in all dimensions. (2) Next, we study the effect of radial symmetry by obtaining dimension estimates for fractional Schrödinger equations with concave phase and radial initial data. Applying a transference principle, dimension estimates are extended to families of abstract dispersive equations. As special cases, we recover the known result for the Beam propagation and also obtain new results for the linearized Boussinesq and the Klein-Gordon propagations in the radial setting. (3) We study analogues of (2) for the $3$-dimensional real hyperbolic space by obtaining dimension estimates for a wide class of dispersive propagations: the Schrödinger, fractional Schrödinger (with convex and concave phases), Beam, linearized Boussinesq, Wave and Klein-Gordon equations. This is the first result of its kind, outside the setting of flat Euclidean geometry. Our arguments are based on an inter-spatial transference principle of geometric-analytic flavour. In the process, we also obtain a quantitative result on the singular sets of Sobolev functions, in the spirit of Žubrinić, which may be of independent interest.

title: Physical limits to stochastic classifiers
abstract: Stochastic physical computers use random transitions between states to process inputs. We quantify their ability to solve distinct tasks as the control parameters of a device vary. For Markov jump devices, we bound the number of classification tasks attainable at a prescribed output margin, with each task defined as a binary labeling of fixed inputs. Combining geometric packing with fluctuation-response inequalities, we bound this number in terms of the control range and dimension, rate sensitivities, output fluctuations, and entropy production. For state and net-current observables, when controls change kinetics without changing thermodynamic forces and energies, the number of tasks is shaped by entropy production and output fluctuations. If the product of their maximum values over the allowed control settings and inputs is too small, the device can perform at most one task. An exactly solvable two-state switch illustrates how sufficient driving and observation time enable barrier tuning to select copying or inversion.

title: Quantum Spectral Estimation with Multiple Initial States: Improved Error and Cost Scaling
abstract: We study quantum spectrum and eigenstate property estimation using multiple initial states and generalized Hadamard tests. Building on the QFAMES (quantum filtering and analysis of multiplicities in eigenvalue spectra) framework, we introduce a new method that samples evolution times independently for each initial-state pair. Under the stated assumptions, when statistical error determines the sampling cost, the total Hamiltonian simulation cost required for fixed-accuracy eigenvalue and observable estimation is independent of the number of initial states, up to logarithmic factors. This improves scalability when many initial states are needed to explore the target eigenspaces. The method also reduces the cost of multiplicity recovery and retains Heisenberg-limited scaling for eigenvalue estimation. Numerical experiments support the predicted statistical error scalings.

title: Decoupled Marginal Sharpening for Training-Free Inference-Time Scaling
abstract: We study how to improve LLM reasoning at inference time without updating model weights or using external reward models. Recent reward-free power-sampling methods define the sequence-level power target $π_α(y\mid x)\propto p_0(y\mid x)^α$, where $α>1$, which increases the relative probability of completions that are already likely under the base model. Existing methods use Metropolis--Hastings or Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) to approximately sample from this target. However, two challenges arise at different levels. At the target level, full-sequence sharpening can concentrate probability on a few exact reasoning--answer trajectories, suppressing alternative paths that support the same answer. At the sampler level, finite-particle SMC can suffer from path collapse when resampling repeatedly duplicates a few high-weight prefixes. To address these challenges, we propose Decoupled Marginal Sharpening (DMS), which separately controls how strongly the model favors particular reasoning paths and how strongly it favors final answers after aggregating support across those paths. At the target level, DMS first samples from a sharpened reasoning distribution, then marginalizes the model's answer probabilities over the resulting weighted reasoning population and sharpens the induced answer marginal. Separate exponents allow mild reasoning sharpening to encourage exploration of diverse paths, followed by stronger answer-marginal sharpening to concentrate probability on answers with greater aggregate support across those paths. At the sampler level, we develop Fully Adapted Annealed SMC, which combines an annealed sequence of power targets with locally fully adapted proposals and predictive ancestor resampling. Experiments on MATH500, GPQA-Diamond, HumanEval, and AIME24/25 across three base models show that DMS achieves the highest mean pass@1 among the compared methods in all tasks.

title: Controller- and Communication-Aware Flexibility Margins for Electric Distribution Networks
abstract: This paper develops a framework for quantifying operational flexibility in radial electric distribution systems under coupled active- and reactive-load uncertainty. Flexibility is defined as the largest scaling of a prescribed uncertainty set that can be accommodated while satisfying network and actuator limits under a given control architecture. We consider a one-sided Euclidean set for robust demand-growth capability, with a direct extension to bidirectional variations. Under LinDistFlow, controllable distributed resources and feeder-head exchange with the upstream grid jointly balance active-power disturbances, while local Volt/VAR feedback regulates reactive power. The resulting affine closed-loop disturbance response admits exact second-order-cone robust counterparts. For fixed Volt/VAR gains, a convex reformulation jointly optimizes the flexibility margin and active-power participation factors, including feeder-head participation. A sparse load-to-generator feedforward map further captures communication constraints. Numerical studies on the Iowa-240 feeder demonstrate how the amount of control authority and communication structure shape the achievable flexibility margin.

title: Cheng's Theorem in the Spectral Setting
abstract: We prove a maximal diameter rigidity theorem for closed 3-dimensional Riemannian manifolds under a spectral lower bound for the Ricci curvature. We show that if $0<γ<2$, $K>0$ and $λ_1(-γΔ+\operatorname{Ric})\geq 2K$, then the optimal bound $\operatorname{diam}(M,g)\leq\fracπ{\sqrt{K}}$ is attained if and only if (M,g) is isometric to the round 3-sphere of constant sectional curvature $K$.

title: Average-Reward Policy Identification from a Single Continuing Trajectory
abstract: In reinforcement learning, an agent must explore an unknown environment to learn how to make good decisions. Unlike methods that can freely sample any state--action pair, an agent learning from a single trajectory must spend additional time navigating between states. It is therefore natural to expect that learning from a single trajectory requires more experience. In this paper, we show that this additional cost is not always necessary. For average-reward reinforcement learning, we develop an algorithm that learns where to collect information while ensuring that the required samples can be obtained efficiently. We establish an upper bound on the number of interactions needed to identify a near-optimal policy. Furthermore, we prove a matching information theoretic lower bound, showing that, for a broad class of environments and at sufficiently high accuracy, learning from a single trajectory is no harder in the worst case than learning with unrestricted access to state action samples. Our results reveal that the additional complexity cost of navigation can be avoided by adapting information gathering requirements to how the environment provides information.

title: Demonstration of a mobile ion-trap quantum device
abstract: Trapped-ion devices are being investigated for transportable applications, including the transfer of exotic charged particles between laboratories and the development of portable quantum technologies. To date, ion transport has been demonstrated only in magnetic (Penning) traps, whereas radiofrequency (Paul) traps are the predominant platform in quantum science. Here, we report the first transport of a few thousand ions confined in a linear Paul trap over distances of several kilometers, with transport durations of 15 and 45 min. These results establish a foundation for mobile trapped-ion quantum devices capable of operating while in motion and may enable the transport of exotic ions in Paul traps between experimental facilities.

title: Cartesian and Curvilinear Anharmonic Frequencies and Intensities: Perturb-then-Diagonalize Polyad Transport and Adiabatic Discrete-Variable Representation
abstract: Anharmonic intensities reveal vibrational coupling that band positions alone cannot determine. We derive explicit second-order infrared transition moments in curvilinear normal coordinates, including kinetic metric derivatives and transport through variational resonance polyads. The vibrational perturbation-to-second-order-then-diagonalization (VP2TD) treatment covers fundamentals, overtones, three-quantum transitions, and hot bands. A general computational platform combines Extended Symmetry-Adapted Local Coordinates (ESALCs), using Cartesian (ESALC-C) or internal (ESALC-I) primitives, with interchangeable quantum-chemical programs and parallel finite differences. Independent oscillator matrices verify the intensity equations; a molecular water check reproduces second-order amplitudes within $8.4\times10^{-8}$ atomic units. Comparisons with established tools reproduce a formaldehyde Fermi polyad within 0.163 cm$^{-1}$ and 0.061 km mol$^{-1}$ and water Raman activities within $10^{-7}$ Angstrom$^6$. For 29 matched formaldehyde rotational line pairs, the predicted hot-to-fundamental intensity ratio, using the measured lower-state energy, is consistent with the nuclear-spin-corrected median: the differences are 3.9% (ESALC-I) and 3.8% (ESALC-C), compared with a 15% uncertainty estimate for individual measured line intensities. Common analytic reference derivatives ensure identical harmonic observables, while internal coordinates reduce and localize intermode anharmonic couplings. Rotation-vibration constants extend the same tensor treatment. An integrated adiabatic discrete-variable representation treats large-amplitude motions, and finite-level partition functions provide anharmonic thermochemistry.

title: Uniform $L^2$-bounds for the $n$-th Calderón commutator on Lipschitz graphs
abstract: We prove that, for every real Lipschitz function $A$ and every integer $n\ge1$, $\|T_{A,n}\|_{L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})}\le C\,\|A'\|_\infty^n$, where $T_{A,n}$ is the $n$-th Calderón commutator and $C$ is an absolute constant. The essential tool is the Coifman--McIntosh--Meyer theorem, applied to a holomorphic family of complex curves, together with the Cauchy integral formula on a contour surrounding the interval of secant slopes. We also include a simpler version of the argument that gives $O(\log n)$ and explains why the contour has the shape it has.

title: Towards Certifiable State Estimation under Observability Degeneracy
abstract: Certifiable optimization provides global optimality guarantees for non-convex state estimation in robotics. However, under severe physical sensing degeneracy, convex Semidefinite Programming relaxations solved via Interior-Point Methods suffer from rank expansion, rendering direct semidefinite solving and spectral rounding algebraically invalid. In this paper, we establish a universal candidate-driven dual certification framework that resolves this challenge without incurring rank expansion. First, from an epigraph perspective, we prove that while sensing degeneracy expands the primal optimal set into a flat equi-cost face, cost tightness and multiplier recovery remain strictly intact, enabling global verification without direct semidefinite solving. Second, we propose an observability-aware local search using solution remapping, coupled with a closed-form dual multiplier recovery scheme that executes in sub-microsecond latency. Third, we derive a model-specific adaptive dual safety threshold parameterized by the minimum non-zero eigenvalue of the observable Hessian and uneradicated residual leakage, preventing false rejections of optimal candidates under weak observability. We validate our universal framework with robust registration under degenerate measurements.

title: Testing Replica Symmetry Breaking in the three-dimensional Edwards-Anderson model by using vanishing fields
abstract: Replica Symmetry Breaking (RSB) theory for spin glasses, which is exact in infinite dimensions, provides detailed predictions for the behavior of these systems. One of these predictions is that vanishing magnetic fields induce chaotic behavior. Here, vanishing has a precise meaning: we refer to an externally applied magnetic field with intensity scaling as $1/\sqrt{N}$, where $N$ is the number of spins in the system. RSB predicts that this chaotic behavior depends only on the probability density function of the overlap, $P(q)$, as computed at zero field. We proceed to test the RSB prediction in the 3D Edwards-Anderson model, by first computing the $P(q)$ numerically in the absence of a magnetic field. We then use this function as input to analytically compute the statistics of the states in the regime of a vanishing magnetic field, using a representation based on the Bolthausen-Sznitman coalescent process (which is exact for the mean-field Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model). This mixed numerical-analytical approach allows us to determine the prediction of RSB for the overlap distribution function measured in the presence of a small vanishing field, as well as the increase in chaoticity as the field strength grows. The above RSB predictions are quantitatively compared with the outcome of numerical simulations of the three-dimensional Edwards-Anderson in the presence of a small vanishing field, finding very good agreement. This agreement provides strong support for the idea that three-dimensional spin glass at zero magnetic field and low temperature is well described by RSB theory.

title: On Complexity of Gaussian Sampling
abstract: We study the number of exact matrix-vector queries needed to sample a centered $d$-dimensional Gaussian with condition number at most $κ$ to total variation error $\varepsilon$. The best known algorithm uses $O(\min\{d,\sqrtκ\log(\frac{d}{\varepsilon})\})$ queries, while the known lower bounds do not grow as $\varepsilon\to0$ and match this bound only for $κ\le d^{1/5-δ}$ at constant accuracy. We introduce a construction based on a hidden determinant sign and prove a lower bound of $Ω\!\left(\min\left\{d,\sqrtκ\log\left(1+\frac{d}{\sqrtκ\,\varepsilon}\right)\right\}\right)$ uniformly for all $d\ge1$, $κ\ge4$, and $0<\varepsilon\le\tfrac{1}{16}$. This bound matches the known upper bound up to constant factors whenever $κ\le d^{2-δ}$ for fixed $δ\in(0,2)$, or $\varepsilon\le d^{-c}$ for fixed $c>0$. We also extend a recent fixed-spectrum construction with a hidden eigenbasis from $κ=2$ to $2\leκ\le d^{1-δ}$, for any fixed $δ\in(0,1)$. This gives an $Ω_δ(\sqrtκ\log d)$ lower bound at constant accuracy that holds even when the spectrum of the precision matrix is known to the algorithm.

title: Giant Wilson loops from Fredholm determinants
abstract: We study large-k symmetric and antisymmetric Wilson loops in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. We represent their generating functions as Fredholm determinants built from the Hermite kernel weighted by a symbol function that encodes the representation. Using the integrable structure of the kernel, we systematically apply the Tracy-Widom approach to derive a closed system of integro-differential equations. The equations are then solved order by order in 1/N by a WKB ansatz, while keeping the symbol function general. We find a closed-form expression for the leading and subleading order contributions to the generating functions. Finally, specializing to the two representations, we perform the large-k saddle-point analysis and find the subleading contribution to the Wilson loop. Our results confirm the previously observed discrepancies with the dual D-brane description of giant Wilson loops.

title: Quantifying privacy risks in foundation model representations of brain MRI
abstract: Pretrained representations are increasingly used to share and reuse information from medical images without exposing the original scans, but it is unclear how much patient-specific information these representations retain. We investigate this question for brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) by evaluating five frozen pretrained encoders spanning different architectures, pretraining objectives, and training domains on two longitudinal T1-weighted datasets, OASIS-2 and MIRIAD. Under an attacker model with access to released embeddings, the corresponding public encoder, and auxiliary MRI scans, we evaluate patient linkage and sensitive-attribute inference. Across the evaluated representations, we observe substantial subject-specific information: rank-1 patient linkage reaches up to 99\% on MIRIAD and exceeds 90\% on OASIS-2 for the highest-risk representation, despite the absence of an identification objective during encoder training. We further show that the released embeddings retain information about a demographic attribute, with recorded-sex prediction reaching balanced accuracy of 90.9\% on OASIS-2 and 95.5\% on MIRIAD. Overall, our results demonstrate that replacing raw brain MRI with learned embeddings does not, by itself, eliminate patient-linkage or attribute-inference risk, and is therefore insufficient on its own to establish anonymity.

title: A Parsec-Scale Transient High-Frequency-Peaked Radio Source in the Very Large Array Sky Survey Brightening and Fading over a Decadal Timescale
abstract: A subset of active galactic nuclei (AGN) manifests as compact radio sources with peaked radio spectra, commonly referred to as peaked-spectrum (PS) sources. Generally, PS sources are interpreted as young radio jets, but the early evolution of the jet is rarely observed and not fully understood. Here, we present VT J182357-234511 (VT J1823-2345), a radio transient in the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS) that resembles a PS source. Notable properties of VT J1823-2345 include: (i) brightening by a factor of 3 between 1996 and 2021 at 1.4 GHz, (ii) peaked spectra with high frequency peaks at $ν_{\mathrm{p,obs}}\gtrsim6\,\mathrm{GHz}$, (iii) a peaked 3 GHz light curve that has been fading since 2023, (iv) a resolved Gaussian (major-axis) size of 0.4 mas in 2024, and (v) a linear polarization fraction $p_{\mathrm{L}}\simeq0.73\%$ at 8.8 GHz with an extreme Faraday rotation measure $\mathrm{RM_{\mathrm{obs}}} \sim +12,000\,\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. On the sky, VT J1823-2345 coincides with a supernova remnant and an F-type star, but no background galaxy is seen. Based on the multi-wavelength properties, we disfavor Galactic transients, explosive extragalactic transients, and blazar variability as plausible explanations. We argue that VT J1823-2345 is consistent with a "short-lived" parsec-scale PS source with a decades-old jet that does not grow into a large-scale radio galaxy. From comparing the full VLASS light curves, we speculate that VT J1823-2345 is similar to many VLASS nuclear transients reported in the literature, which may represent an emerging class of transient radio jets, perhaps related to episodic AGN activity or jetted tidal disruption events.

title: Smoothness criterion for Fano orbifolds and bases of Lagrangian fibrations
abstract: We establish a smoothness criterion for Fano varieties with quotient singularities. As an application, we show that if $X\to B$ is a Lagrangian fibration from a compact hyper-Kähler manifold and $B$ has quotient singularities, then $B$ is a projective space.

title: Hindsight-Privileged RLVR: Single-Rollout Token Credit Without Group Sampling
abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) trains language models from checked task outcomes, but assigning a terminal reward to individual reasoning tokens or actions remains difficult. Group-relative methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) sample several attempts per prompt, but lose their reward-based learning signal when all attempts receive the same outcome. We propose Hindsight-Privileged RLVR (HP-RLVR), a single-rollout method that turns a completed trajectory's own future into token-level update weights. The generating policy snapshot scores each eligible token under its causal history and under a hindsight context containing the realized future and verifier feedback. A normalized Jensen--Shannon divergence between the two views weights the reward relative to a historical baseline, yielding bounded token credit for both successful and failed attempts, with no reference solution or learned critic. In paired Qwen3-8B runs over a shared $100$-step schedule, HP-RLVR trains $1.21\times$, $1.46\times$, and $2.30\times$ faster than GRPO on mathematics, code generation, and ALFWorld, using one eighth the rollouts per prompt. Accuracy is comparable overall, with HP-RLVR ahead on mathematics at all three sizes and GRPO ahead on code and ALFWorld. In ALFWorld, $43.2\%$ (4B) and $49.0\%$ (8B) of GRPO's gradient-norm records are zero, versus none for HP-RLVR.

title: Structural identification in general crystalline systems via Voronoi cell topology
abstract: Widely used methods for identifying crystal structure in atomistic simulations are limited in practice to a handful of simple structures, leaving many important crystalline systems without automated classification techniques. Voronoi topology analysis offers a route to classifying arbitrary crystalline and defect environments, but realizing this potential first requires enumerating the Voronoi cell topologies that can arise under thermal perturbation of a structure of interest. We present an algorithm that deterministically enumerates all Voronoi cell topologies arising from generic infinitesimal perturbations of an arbitrary crystal structure, producing structural classifiers that extend automated identification to general crystalline systems. We demonstrate the approach on several structures of general interest.

title: $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth approximation of mod $k$ integral cycles
abstract: We prove that every mod $k$ integral cycle $T$ of sufficiently high codimension in an oriented Riemannian manifold $\mathcal{M}$ can be approximated in flat norm by a cycle which is a $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifold $Σ$ of nearly the same area, up to a singular set of codimension 5. If in addition $T$ belongs to a mod $k$ homology class admitting an embedded $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth manifold representative, then $Σ$ can be taken fully regular, up to the codimension one stratum of classical singularities. This extends the smooth approximation theory to cycles with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ in stable regimes. Moreover, we provide examples showing the impossibility of locally approximating minimizing cycles by smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth submanifolds, even in homology classes with smooth or $\mathbb{Z}_k$-smooth representatives.

title: Separation of variables for coupled radiative perturbations of Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes
abstract: We extend Hintz's separation of variables for radiative gravitational and electromagnetic perturbations from Kerr-Newman to Kerr-Newman-de Sitter black holes. On subextremal backgrounds with nonzero rotation and charge, an explicit algebraic matrix transformation yields coupled two-component radial and angular ordinary differential systems linked by a common separation constant. The transformation is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both signs of spin weight. For real frequencies, we establish a complete angular mode decomposition. We also translate regularity at the future black hole outer and cosmological horizons into ingoing and outgoing boundary conditions, respectively, for the separated radial systems. These results show that exact separation of the coupled radiative equations extends beyond asymptotically flat Kerr-Newman spacetime.

title: OLiVES: An Outdoor Low-Light Video Benchmark for Enhancement and Segmentation
abstract: Low-light video processing remains an underexplored problem in computer vision, primarily due to the scarcity of high-quality ground-truth data. Existing public datasets exhibit several limitations, including restricted motion diversity, limited scene coverage, weak degradations, reliance on auxiliary modalities such as event data, and misalignment between low-light inputs and ground truth. Furthermore, current datasets typically address either low-light enhancement or scene understanding, whereas these tasks should be considered jointly. We introduce \textbf{OLiVES}, a benchmark dataset for outdoor low-light videos with dynamic scenes, designed to support both low-light video enhancement (LLVE) and video object segmentation (VOS). The dataset addresses key content gaps by incorporating a diverse range of natural textures, animals, occlusions, dynamic activities, and close-up scenes. To the best of our knowledge, OLiVES is the first outdoor low-light video dataset captured using professional cinema-grade cameras. It provides over 25,000 aligned normal- and low-light frame pairs, along with over 46,000 VOS annotations. We benchmark state-of-the-art LLVE and VOS methods on OLiVES and show that training on it improves performance on both tasks. The OLiVES project page is available at: https://anonymous-OLiVES.github.io/.

title: Graph-Enhanced Disease Trajectory Discovery and Temporal Endpoint Forecasting from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
abstract: Longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) can reveal disease-progression structure, while useful forecasting requires leakage-controlled discovery, censor-aware outcomes, and inspectable trajectory evidence. We developed a graph-enhanced framework in MIMIC-IV v3.1 that splits patients before graph construction, learns train-only consecutive-admission transitions, and freezes endpoint-specific branching-motif policies selected on validation data. The final catalog contained 99,527 motifs, and a time-aware Transformer retrieved at most 24 patient-compatible motifs per endpoint through endpoint-specific cross-attention. Across five training seeds, micro-AUPRC increased from 0.9330 to 0.9357, while event-time MAE decreased from 676.9 to 657.7 days (reduction 19.2 days; 95% paired patient-cluster bootstrap CI, 13.8-24.8). Timing effects were heterogeneous: MAE worsened for events within 730 days but improved by 58.9 days for events occurring after 730 days. In an exploratory internal temporal split, branch conditioning reduced conditional event-time MAE by 26.9 days (95% CI, 23.0-30.8) without evidence of better micro-AUPRC. Corrected survival evaluation over the supported 0-2,555-day interval did not establish macro C-index or integrated Brier score superiority over a matched history-only discrete-hazard model. A directed, degree-matched GNN repair substantially improved unseen-edge discovery, yet replacing GNN-derived scores within fixed motif identities did not improve downstream forecasting. These results position branching motifs as structured trajectory context whose main value is long-range timing support rather than uniformly stronger endpoint discrimination, survival prediction, or causal explanation.

title: ReaDy: Recurrent States as Dynamic Context for Speculative Drafting in Hybrid Linear Attention Large Language Models
abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive generation by drafting multiple tokens per step, yet feature-based drafters rely on target hidden features whose contextual emphasis may not align with the needs of subsequent draft positions. Hybrid linear attention (HLA) models maintain compact recurrent states that accumulate historical associations, offering an efficient source of complementary context for speculative drafting. We introduce ReaDy, the first speculative decoding method, to the best of our knowledge, to leverage HLA recurrent states for position-specific context retrieval during drafting. ReaDy equips each draft position with a learned query to retrieve supplementary context directly from the target's committed recurrent states. A lightweight state reader integrates this context into draft representations through residual updates, while low-rank state reads and fused operators keep additional computation and I/O overhead low. Building on DSpark's parallel backbone and sequential prediction head, ReaDy employs a lightweight two-stage adaptation strategy, with reader capacity, state sources, and residual placement examined through ablation studies. Across seven benchmarks spanning mathematics, code generation, and dialogue, ReaDy achieves an average $3.16\times$ decoding speedup over autoregressive decoding with Qwen3.8-27B on a single NVIDIA B200 GPU. It outperforms DSpark on every benchmark, improving throughput by 7.97% and acceptance length by 8.50% on average. Our code is available at https://github.com/StartLuxLabs/ReaDy.

title: Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning with Human Interventions for Precise Robotic Manipulation
abstract: Long-horizon precise manipulation produces mixed-quality data for post-training vision-language-action (VLA) models: even successful demonstrations and intervention-assisted rollouts may contain detours, hesitations, failed attempts, and imperfect recoveries. The key challenge is to identify which action chunks actually advance the task, rather than uniformly cloning or discarding imperfect trajectories. We propose Graph-Reweighted Behavior Cloning (GR-BC), an offline iterative post-training framework that builds a task-conditioned goal-reachability graph over demonstrations and iteratively collected rollouts, including both successful and failed episodes with human interventions. Reverse graph search computes minimal remaining steps to task success within the dataset support, and each action chunk is weighted by how much its execution reduces this potential. This consequence-based weighting reuses recoverable segments from failed trajectories, leverages interventions as recovery paths, and down-weights locally regressive chunks even inside successful trajectories. New rollouts are incorporated by appending them to the graph and rerunning search, without training a reward model, action-conditioned critic, or progress predictor. Across four precise manipulation tasks and three VLA backbones, GR-BC improves single-round supervised fine-tuning and reaches 91% success after a few offline iterations, without trajectory comparisons or progress labels. More details and videos are available at: https://gr-bc.github.io

title: A Step-Like Transition Underlying the Life and Death of Galaxies
abstract: How galaxies stop forming stars is a complex and central problem in astrophysics. Numerous physical mechanisms have been proposed, yet a simple, unified framework connecting these mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we derive a step-function quenching response from the fundamental principle of gas mass conservation, governed by the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales. This response also enables the gas-supply timescale to be inferred from the observed quenched fraction. Applying this method to approximately 350,000 galaxies, we find a characteristic gas-supply timescale of ~1 Gyr, reveal distinct inside-out and outside-in quenching signatures associated with supermassive black holes and dark matter halos, respectively, and identify galaxies with intermediate stellar surface mass densities as occupying a critical state for quenching and rejuvenation. Our work establishes a unified physical framework in which a simple step-function response captures how diverse physical processes regulate galaxy quenching and the resumption of star formation through their effects on the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales.

title: Modelling the 6.7 GHz Methanol Flaring in G358.93-0.03 Using the Maxwell-Bloch Framework
abstract: We model selected 6.7 GHz methanol flare profiles in G358.93-0.03 using the one-dimensional Maxwell-Bloch framework. The 2019 non-periodic flare, associated with an accretion burst, produced complex single-dish light curves characterized by sharp rises, multiple peaks, secondary structure, and extended decays. For six representative velocity channels, we model each light curve as a sum of scaled intensity responses from effective emitting systems driven by phenomenological pump pulses of fixed width but with component-dependent background rates, amplitudes, and arrival times. The inferred initial inverted column densities correspond to characteristic superradiance timescales $T_{R,0} \simeq 0.3$-$1.4~{\rm d}$, which are shorter than the adopted dephasing and relaxation timescales, $T_2 = 6.9~{\rm d}$ and $T_1 = 144.4~{\rm d}$. The fitted components therefore lie in the fast-transient superradiance regime. Existent VLBI observations motivate the possibility that a single-dish velocity channel blends emission from multiple unresolved flaring regions, although these observations are not used as direct fitting constraints. Although the decomposition is not unique, it provides a physically motivated description of the complex flare morphology within a unified Maxwell-Bloch framework.

title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
abstract: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. We bound the mass that a single object can eject and sum it over realistic models of the Milky Way and of other types of galaxies. For gravitational atoms, with realistic stellar populations and stellar evolution, the stars of the Milky Way deplete at most $ε^{\rm GA}_\star\simeq3\times10^{-9}$ of its halo, and the pump is equally negligible in other galaxies. The central black hole, Sgr A$^*$, could reach $ε^{\rm GA}\sim10^{-3}$, but only for a boson mass disfavoured by ultrafaint dwarf galaxies and beyond the validity of the perturbative treatment, where only a geometric bound on the dark matter flux is available. For boson stars feeding on the rest of the halo, these would radiate at most $\sim3\times10^{-5}$ of the Milky-Way halo and $0.1\%$ of a DF2-like one.

title: On Meeks' conjecture on disjoint minimal graphs
abstract: We study disjoint solution pairs $(u,D)$ to the minimal surface equation in $\mathbb{R}^n$, with $u=0$ on $\partial D.$ A conjecture of W. Meeks states that at most two such pairs can exist in $\mathbb{R}^n.$ We confirm the conjecture in two complementary cases. For $n\in\{2,3,4,5,6\},$ we prove it under a superlinearity assumption. In dimension $n=2,$ we establish the result under a suitable sublinearity assumption. We also derive estimates on the asymptotic angle of domains supporting nontrivial solutions for $n\geq 3.$

title: VascuSR: Iterative Anatomy-Aware Diffusion for CT Super-Resolution
abstract: Generative super-resolution (SR) can recover sharp detail in computed tomography (CT) images from severely downsampled observations, but the missing high-frequency content is not uniquely determined by the low-resolution input. Consequently, visually plausible reconstructions may contain anatomically unsupported vascular detail, such as missing, spurious, or incorrectly connected vessels. To overcome this challenge, we introduce VascuSR, an iterative anatomy-aware diffusion framework that combines image reconstruction with explicit 3D vascular guidance. First, to provide richer anatomical guidance, we use an explicit 3D vascular representation that captures structural information beyond individual slices. This representation also simplifies vascular refinement by allowing a lightweight 3D generative refiner to focus on vascular structure rather than complex CT appearance. Second, to guide slice-wise SR, a lightweight anatomy controller injects the refined structure into the diffusion decoder, while iterative feedback updates this guidance from each new SR volume. On re-annotated MSD Task08 and HVM datasets, VascuSR outperforms interpolation and learning-based SR baselines in segmentation accuracy (Dice and clDice) and 3D vascular structure (connectivity and mean centerline distance), while maintaining image quality comparable to its SR backbone. Compared with learning-based baselines, VascuSR reduces class-averaged connected-component counts by over 20% on both datasets and mean centerline distance by over 10% on MSD.

title: Claw-Free and Line Graph Edge Deletion on Block Graphs
abstract: Edge deletion problems ask for the fewest edges whose deletion gives a graph with a specified property. We study two such problems on block graphs. First making the graph claw-free, and second making it a line graph. Since every line graph is claw-free, the second problem is at least as difficult as the first. We show that on block graphs the two optimum values are always equal, and both are attained by the line graph of a forest. The main step is a completion argument, in which starting from any claw-free solution, we put back edges to get some nice structure inside each block still maintaining the claw-free property. This reduces both edge-deletion problems to the same problem of selecting vertices within the blocks of the input graph. We solve it by dynamic programming in $O(n+m)$ time, which also produces an optimal deletion set and a forest whose line graph is what remains after the completion argument. We also extend the method to $K_{1,r+1}$-free edge deletion for every fixed $r$.

title: Measurement of electromagnetic transition form factors in two-photon collisions at BESIII
abstract: The muon anomalous magnetic moment, $a_μ= (g-2)_μ/2$, shows a sizeable discrepancy between Standard Model (SM) predictions and direct measurements, hinting at either New Physics or limitations in modeling low-energy strong interactions. As the uncertainty in the SM predictions currently exceeds the experimental uncertainty by a substantial margin, further improvements in theoretical precision are essential to clarify the origin of this discrepancy. The SM theoretical uncertainty is dominated by hadronic processes. The hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution relies on highly accurate data for hadron production via two-photon fusion. Operating at $\sqrt{s}=3.773\,\text{GeV}$ with over $20\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity, the BESIII experiment is ideally suited to probe these processes at small momentum transfers. By precisely measuring channels like $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-π^0$ and $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-π^0π^0$, BESIII provides the critical experimental input necessary to sharpen the SM prediction and clarify the true nature of the $a_μ$ anomaly.

title: A Two-Level Clinical Novelty Prioritization Framework for Disease Trajectories Discovered from Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
abstract: Graph-based analysis of electronic health records (EHRs) yields disease-trajectory catalogs, but structural support does not establish semantic novelty. We present a two-level framework to prioritize 99,527 branching motifs previously discovered by an upstream patient-disjoint, train-only MIMIC-IV v3.1 pipeline and frozen after validation-based catalog selection. The framework separates path-level and node-to-endpoint semantic sparsity from reliability-adjusted clinical priority. Three deterministic textualizations per motif or node-target pair were embedded with BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5 and calibrated against 166,972 pre-2023 PubMed references using mean top-20 cosine distance. Positive recombination occurred in 8.63% of motifs and had negligible effect on global ranking, whereas specificity and support/GNN reliability terms changed clinical-priority ordering. Robustness analyses across neighbor counts, templates, encoders, generic-label taxonomies, score settings, PrimeKG, and corrected density-based RND showed that broad ordering was more stable than hard top-k membership. A semantic-dose analysis did not support a monotonic relation between score and forecasting benefit after endpoint and token-count adjustment (1.96 days per SD; 95% CI, -0.75 to 4.68). In the frozen catalog-q90 high-semantic subgroup, branch-enhanced forecasting reduced conditional event-time MAE by 20.1 days (95% CI, 13.3-27.0) and sMAPE by 2.37 percentage points (95% CI, 1.81-2.93), while discrimination and endpoint-ranking differences were inconclusive. Corrected RND showed low tail agreement with the primary score (Spearman rho = 0.430; q90 Jaccard = 0.125) despite a similar aggregate timing association. These findings support representation-aware, uncertainty-aware literature-relative prioritization of discovered trajectories rather than causal discovery or clinician-adjudicated novelty.

title: Effective equidistribution of polynomial trajectories in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$
abstract: For a fixed matrix-polynomial trajectory in $\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb R)/\operatorname{SL}_3(\mathbb Z)$, we give a necessary and sufficient intrinsic Diophantine condition for its time averages to equidistribute at a power rate on its homogeneous orbit closure. The condition uses a lattice in the space of polynomial functions on the normalized orbit-closure group, each admitting a representative of total degree at most two in the matrix entries. These polynomial tests have a common degree bound of two, independent of the curve degree and optimal in general. The proof begins with a classification of the possible orbit-closure groups and derives lower bounds for polynomial coefficient vectors from the intrinsic condition. It combines quantitative nilmanifold equidistribution, unipotent tangent approximation, and effective flow estimates, with arithmetic separation and quantitative nondivergence controlling cusp excursions and periodic-orbit obstructions.

title: Bayesian Learning to Select Fair Classifiers
abstract: Evaluations of classifiers (AI or human or agents) often assume a batch setting in which every agent produces labels on every example in a test set, which can be expensive or impractical in many contexts. This motivates online policies that adaptively select agents to query as examples arrive and update policies as outcomes are observed. We study the problem of selecting, in an online stream, the agent that best balances (i) predictive performance and (ii) subgroup fairness of a sensitive attribute, and that allows for delayed observations of true class labels. We formulate this as a Bayesian multi-armed bandit problem using Thompson Sampling, explicitly balancing accuracy and fairness. We conduct empirical evaluations on real-world datasets spanning problems involving tabular classifiers, large language models, and human labelers, demonstrating substantial reductions in regret relative to baselines. Our theoretical contributions include guarantees on the performance of the selected agent that incorporate both the accuracy and fairness aspects of the problem.

title: Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
abstract: The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
abstract: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation. Recent methods combine this signal with GRPO. They use GRPO for update directions and the teacher for signal scaling. However, we demonstrate a more effective integration within PPO. Specifically, we identify complementary positional dynamics: privileged information enhances a critic's value-prediction accuracy toward the response's end, whereas self-teacher guidance is strong initially, drops mid-generation, and rebounds finally. These insights motivate Value-Augmented Self-Distillation Policy Optimization (VASPO), wherein a self-teacher and critic evaluate identical privileged information at student-generated prefixes. The critic computes token-level PPO advantages from predicted continuation returns, while the self-teacher modulates selected positive advantages via bounded probability ratios. Across six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, VASPO improves mean accuracy over PPO by 2.59 and 1.81 percentage points on Qwen3-4B and OLMo3-7B variants, respectively, and achieves the highest mean accuracy among evaluated methods on Knights and Knaves. Our code is available at https://github.com/cii030/VASPO.

title: Effect of deep-trap density of states for a-Si:H layers on HIT cell performances: Modeling Framework
abstract: In this work, an aSi and cSi heterojunction solar cell with an intrinsic layer is simulated using AFORS-HET software. The study focuses on the role of the electronic density of states DOS of the amorphous emitter, p type aSiH, in governing the performance of the HIT cell and the electronic transfer across the heterointerface. It is found that the DOS of the p type aSiH emitter can cause an unfavorable recombination and trapping effect, which becomes more severe and difficult to avoid when the bulk dangling-bond density in the a-Si emitter approaches or exceeds the doping concentration. An increase in deep trap density beyond a critical value causes a drop in the built in voltage and shifts the depletion layer into p type aSi. This situation leads to a sharp decline in HIT cell performance, namely the open circuit voltage and the fill factor, and to the appearance of an S shaped IV characteristic. The simulation results suggest that the emitter activation energy needs to be optimized to achieve high efficiency. Under optimal conditions, holes accumulate near the heterojunction interface, leading to the formation of an inversion layer. This paper presents a physical mechanism for recombination processes within the emitter and concludes with the optimized parameters required to achieve a HIT cell efficiency comparable to Sanyo record of 23 percent on a thin silicon wafer.

title: The Wealth of Agents: Scaling Agentic AI Across Developers
abstract: Today's agentic systems are typically designed, built, and deployed by single developers with full control over all participating agents. While this simplifies development, it limits the potential scale of agentic systems. We study multi-developer agentic systems (MDAs) which enable developers to collaboratively build agentic systems to push frontier capability beyond what any individual developer could achieve alone. We construct empirical and theoretical models of developers to compare MDAs with single-developer agentic systems (SDAs). On GAIA, a general assistant benchmark, a population of specialized developers whose individual agents do not exceed 35% accuracy reaches 70% when their agents are combined in an MDA. This MDA performs 12 percentage points above the median general-purpose SDA built with several times each specialist's development budget. Our theoretical models show how MDAs can incentivize specialization and encourage more efficient use of aggregated developer resources. Put together, our results make a preliminary case for MDAs as a new scaling axis by enabling developers with diverse capabilities and resources to advance agentic AI collaboratively.

title: Probabilistic AI models outperform numerical weather prediction models on record breaking heat extremes
abstract: AI weather prediction (AIWP) models have emerged as a key complement to physics-based numerical weather prediction (NWP) models, and now often outperform them on aggregate skill. Yet, several studies report that physics-based models still forecast extreme events better, in particular record-breaking extremes, based on the evaluation of deterministic forecasts. Here we evaluate heat extreme forecasts from probabilistic AIWP models over global land and show that they clearly outperform the ECMWF IFS ensemble, both raw and post-processed, including for record-breaking events, in all regions and at all lead times considered. AIWP models better forecast the occurrence and intensity of extremes, are better calibrated in the tail and miss fewer records. Station observations confirm these results. We argue that many reported AIWP limitations stem from unsuitable verification choices, specifically comparing deterministic forecasts that target different quantities. Instead, a fair evaluation of extremes necessitates probabilistic verification.

title: Universally extendible characters
abstract: Let theta be an ordinary character or a Brauer character of a finite group N. We show that theta extends to every overgroup $G=G_θ\trianglerighteq N$ if and only if Z(N) <= Ker(theta) and the deflated character of Inn(N) extends to Aut(N)_theta. This equivalence is compatible with fields of values. A similar investigation for extensions from subnormal subgroups leads to a new characteristic subgroup of N.

title: Tulva: Practical Asynchronous Threshold FHE
abstract: We present Tulva, a practical threshold FHE scheme which equips a base FHE scheme with an asynchronous threshold decryption mechanism in a modular way. Our scheme simultaneously (1) is compatible with virtually any base FHE scheme and leaves its ciphertexts unchanged apart from an appended random tag, (2) supports a wide range of threshold profiles $(t,K)$ and ring degrees $\geq 256$ with 6-25 bits partial decryption per plaintext bit, and (3) achieves security in the presence of partial decryption queries on challenge ciphertexts based on the standard LWE assumption. We provide an open-source implementation, benchmark its threshold decryption performance and evaluate the end-to-end costs for typical privacy-preserving Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) use cases. For 16-out-of-512 threshold and a publicly preprocessed ciphertext, computing secret-dependent partial decryption and public share combination requires only 3.7 ms and 0.5 ms, respectively, on commodity hardware. Compared with the state-of-the-art synchronous scheme [Zyskind et al., CCS'25], we replace their ciphertext-independent yet interactive preparation of secret-correlated randomness with a public, ciphertext-dependent 0.5 s preprocessing step, eliminate interaction in the online phase while maintaining similar decryption time on the same machine, and support 32$\times$ more total users.

title: Anyons at impurities: Fractional charge measurement and "wrong sign" binding
abstract: Recent photoluminescence experiments in twisted MoTe$_2$ have reported signatures of anyons binding to trapped trions. The measured binding energies near the fractional Chern insulators at fillings of $ν=-2/3$ and $-3/5$ have a ratio close to the fractional-charge ratio $5/3$, even though such scaling is not generally guaranteed for the expected short-range trion-anyon interaction. We model the trapped trion as a fixed impurity, and investigate anyon-impurity binding using a lowest-Landau-level model with exact diagonalization and Jain wavefunctions. Surprisingly, we find that the anyon-impurity binding energy ratio between $ν=-2/3$ and $-3/5$ is close to $5/3$ for either short- or long-ranged impurity-electron interactions. However, the ratio departs strongly from the charge ratio at intermediate ranges or different Jain states. Remarkably, we also uncover "wrong-sign" binding, whereby both quasiholes and quasiparticles can bind to either sign of a short-range impurity potential by selecting orbital channels with favorable local density oscillations. Our findings show that localized excitons or trions can be used to probe the internal density profile of anyons.

title: Growth-induced trade-off between polarity, electrical isolation, and structural quality in AlN grown on Si(111) by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy
abstract: We investigate the effects of substrate temperature and Al flux, at a fixed N flux, on the polarity, electrical properties, and structural quality of AlN films grown on high-resistivity Si(111) by plasma-assisted molecular beam epitaxy. N-rich conditions result in relatively highly resistive Al-polar AlN/Si, whereas Al-rich conditions promote N-polarity and improved structural quality but simultaneously lead to increased p-type conductivity of AlN/Si stacks, consistent with unintentional Al doping of the Si substrate during AlN growth. Increasing the substrate temperature further improves the structural quality while enhancing the unwanted conductivity, revealing a growth-induced trade-off among polarity, electrical isolation, and structural quality. By reducing the substrate temperature to 575°C while maintaining slightly Al-rich conditions, an N-polar AlN/Si stack with a sheet resistance of 276 kΩ/sq is achieved. These results provide guidelines for optimizing AlN/Si templates for various nitride device heterostructures.

title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics
abstract: Existing robot policy memories typically evolve with observation sequences, implicitly treating each update as the same amount of physical time. Yet identical observation histories can span different durations and require different actions, exposing physical time as a missing dimension of policy memory. We introduce Temporal Flow Policy (TFP), which learns memory dynamics to retain past events and evolve the memory state over measured time intervals. Observations and prior memory determine the content and time scales of each transition; elapsed time determines how far the state advances. TFP conditions diffusion and flow-matching policies through this memory state and is trained with their native imitation objectives. We evaluate TFP with Diffusion Policy and $π_{0.5}$ through controlled comparisons of memory designs. These experiments show that successful timing depends on both measured intervals and retained history. TFP achieves higher average success than the recurrent and state-space memories we equip with the same intervals and than a variant that feeds the interval to a learned gate. Memory readouts recover the time since an event and motion information after occlusion. Changing the supplied intervals systematically delays or advances actions, linking time inputs to behavior. Real-robot tasks requiring timing or memory, together with LIBERO evaluations, demonstrate benefits in physical and general manipulation. These results suggest viewing robot memory not as stored observation history, but as a state that retains past events and evolves with physical time.

title: The Physics Is the Network: Fast, Training-Free Neural Emulation
abstract: Neural emulation need not require learning a substitute for known physics. We investigate PolyNets that couple a continuous-time neural representation of polynomial dynamics with a simple recurrent network for discrete-time integration. When the governing coefficients are known, the resulting tensor graph requires no training and preserves the prescribed numerical scheme while enabling efficient hardware execution and parallel simulation. Using the one-dimensional Korteweg-de Vries equation, we compare PolyNet with CPU and GPU finite-difference Runge-Kutta solvers and three trained neural models: a state-map emulator, a physics-informed predictor, and a learned-tendency integrator. Analytical soliton solutions provide a reference for amplitude and phase errors across grid resolutions, 10^6 dispersively scaled time steps, ensembles of up to 10^4 trajectories, and varying initial amplitudes. PolyNet achieves accuracy comparable to the numerical solvers, including at amplitudes outside the learned models' training conditions. It combines this fidelity with high GPU throughput, approximately constant over the tested resolution range, and favorable ensemble scaling.

title: Lluna: Collaborative Unimodal Models for Missing-Modality Inference
abstract: Pretrained unimodal models offer a flexible route to multimodal prediction through collaboration, but this collaboration can become less accurate than a surviving unimodal model when modalities are missing. We study this setting using fixed surviving-model anchors and find that collaborative gains can weaken or reverse as inputs disappear, even when the anchor's own input is unchanged. Our diagnostics further reveal reduced recovery of modality-specific information after aggregation and state-dependent collaborative representations. We propose Lluna, which combines a direct private prediction path from adapted unimodal features with a common graph-based collaboration branch that provides a residual correction. Progressive Collaboration Consistency organizes richer-to-poorer guidance along single-modality removals, aligning normalized common representations while task supervision adapts predictions to the available evidence. Across eight datasets spanning affective computing, scene understanding, and medical prediction, Lluna achieves the best evaluated average performance over non-full input states, improving Mean-Missing by 4.26\% on average relative to the strongest evaluated baseline. The fixed-anchor diagnostic also shows positive gains in mean collaboration under minimal inputs on all eight tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/AIFrontierLab/Lluna.

title: JetStream: Generating Verified Query Accelerators for Existing Database Systems
abstract: Recent work has shown that LLMs can synthesize highly specialized database systems for fixed workloads, but these systems replace the DBMS's native storage and assume static data: users must migrate their data, often give up ad-hoc queries, and lose acceleration once the data changes. We present JetStream, which instead generates query-specific accelerators that extend an existing DBMS. Given a set of parametrized query templates, a staged agentic workflow synthesizes accelerators that run directly over the DBMS's native tables and may maintain custom auxiliary state, while the DBMS remains responsible for storage, transactions, recovery, and all other queries. A fixed, engine-neutral substrate handles engine-specific hooks and keeps auxiliary state transactionally consistent under writes. JetStream generates two kinds of accelerators: tested accelerators, which may use any optimization and are validated by differential testing, and verified accelerators which trade some performance for a machine-checked proof that every answer satisfies a trusted specification derived from the SQL. On TPC-H at SF=20, JetStream achieves a $315 \times$ geomean read speedup over DuckDB ($93 \times$ verified) and retains $120 \times$ under a continuous update stream of 10,000 modified rows per second.

title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance
abstract: We demonstrate that the one-time measurement scheme is more consistent than the standard two-time measurement scheme with respect to the fundamental symmetry of entanglement, namely entanglement-assisted invariance (envariance). In particular, the work statistics obtained from the one-time measurement scheme arise naturally as a direct consequence of envariance for any driving unitary, without involving an explicit measurement postulate, whereas the analogous identification for the two-time measurement scheme is possible only for a Haar-measure-zero set of unitaries. This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.
